DeepSeek.content:
# Amid the global open-source war, how many AI projects have been brought back down to their true unimpressive state?

每日资本论2026-10-26 11:01

The core of the game amid the global open-source wave of large models is the scramble for discourse power of the ecosystem.

Once open source loses the support of its competitive position, the retreat speed can be faster than the expansion speed.

The global large model industry is now in a fiercely competitive landscape.

On October 20, DeepSeek released an announcement that shocked the global AI community: it fully open-sourced DeepInfer, its internally native inference framework that supports large-scale online inference services, and simultaneously released the production-grade Token codec component deepseek-recipe. The two code repositories were launched on the GitHub developer community at the same time, corresponding to Apache 2.0 and MIT licenses respectively, opening the commercially usable, modifiable and redistributable underlying infrastructure code to developers worldwide. Media commented on this move as — DeepSeek open-sourced its own "money printer", making it a real OpenAI.

Among the global top large model manufacturers, DeepSeek has thus become the first enterprise to make its native inference framework in the production environment public. Prior to this, inference scheduling, operator optimization, and Token alignment logic had long been regarded by MaaS service providers as core commercial secrets to maintain the premium of official APIs and widen the deployment cost gap with the community.

This open source move is not a simple technical gift. In the technical document "DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Large-Scale Inference Deployment Practice" released together, DeepSeek disclosed the operation baseline of its own online cluster: relying on the DeepInfer scheduling system, a single cluster carries about 155 trillion Token request traffic per day, and the peak throughput after conversion is close to 17.94 billion Tokens per second. According to the API pricing standard in off-peak hours, the revenue corresponding to each computing card per hour reaches 38 US dollars.

This system natively supports two hardware routes: NVIDIA SM100 GPU and Huawei Ascend 950 NPU. The supporting deepseek-recipe is responsible for unifying the dialogue message format, prompt encoding, streaming output parsing, tool call and JSON Schema structured return, so that the call experience after private deployment by cloud manufacturers can be consistent with DeepSeek's official API.

While the news spread, the global open source track has entered a high-density release cycle. Just two days after DeepSeek's open source move, iFlytek, another leading domestic large model enterprise, announced the official release of Spark X2.6, which achieves breakthroughs in code and agent capabilities based on fully domestic computing power for the first time, and also announced that it will continue to carry out open source operations. Six months ago, it launched AstronClaw, the first domestic enterprise-level open source and self-hosted AI skill management platform.

The pace on the overseas side is equally rapid. Meta's Llama series continues to iterate weight versions, Google continues to supplement inference optimization suites after the Gemma series of lightweight models, NVIDIA led an 800 million US dollar investment to support Reflection AI to launch the Beam large model, and completed the acquisition of Hugging Face at the same time.

It is worth mentioning that Jensen Huang took the lead in uniting 25 technology companies to release the open letter "Open Weights and U.S. AI Leadership", advocating to maintain the survival of the open source weight ecosystem and opposing one-size-fits-all regulatory bans. Microsoft, Meta and Mistral are all on this joint signature list, while Anthropic and Google's closed source team still adhere to the closed source path — the rift between the open source and closed source routes inside Silicon Valley has been publicly placed on the table.

The unavoidable question then arises: Why have global large model enterprises collectively turned to open source in just two years? If open source means that model weights, inference tools and underlying codes are open to the public, which means anyone can download, fine-tune, deploy and transform them, is the moat of traditional API sales disappearing?

## 01

To understand this wave of AI open source, the most appropriate reference sample is not the current large model, but two classic games that have been written into the history of the software industry: Microsoft's decades-long strategy of swinging repeatedly between closure and open source, and Google's commercial experiment that Android quickly occupied the smartphone market relying on open source strategy.

The entanglement between Microsoft and open source is the best historical negative to understand this competition. From the end of the 20th century to the beginning of the 21st century, Microsoft regarded Linux and GPL as a fundamental threat to the Windows authorization model. Then CEO Steve Ballmer once called Linux a "cancer". But after Satya Nadella took over as CEO in 2014, the trend reversed.

In June 2018, Microsoft acquired GitHub for 7.5 billion US dollars. Nadella's wording in the official statement was: "Microsoft is a developer-first company. By joining GitHub, we have strengthened our commitment to developer freedom, openness and innovation." He also said the sentence that was repeatedly quoted later: "Microsoft is all-in on open source." The reason why Microsoft embraced open source as if it had "returned to its original form" is not that open source suddenly became morally correct, but that its profit center shifted from Windows authorization to Azure cloud services, and a large number of Linux and open source workloads run on the cloud. Without supporting open source, Azure would only be a "Windows Only" cloud, which has no chance of winning in the cloud war.

The Android system built by Google in the mobile Internet era verified the power of open source expansion even earlier. After the release of iPhone in 2007, Google had almost no foothold in the mobile operating system. If Android was closed source, no mobile phone manufacturer would have reason to abandon the system they were using to bet on a newcomer. Google's choice was to open source the underlying code of Android, attract Samsung, HTC, Motorola and other manufacturers to enter the market collectively with zero authorization cost, and fight against iOS by the way of "uniting all manufacturers".

But Google's "open source" was designed in layers from the very beginning: the underlying code was opened to expand the device base, and GMS — Play Store, Gmail, Maps — which truly generates continuous profits, has always been closed source and firmly controlled by Google. The victory of Android is the victory of the business architecture of making scale through the open layer and making profits through the closed source layer, rather than the victory of the pure open source concept.

In short, the underlying logic of Android is to open the underlying layer to compete for ecological seats, and close the traffic entrance to hold the monetization channel. Applied to today's large model industry, DeepSeek's open source of DeepInfer this time is essentially an upgraded version that reproduces this logic: the model weights have been opened before, and now it further opens the inference scheduling middle layer, fills the most expensive and highest threshold link in the deployment link, reduces the cost of cloud manufacturers, government and enterprise customers to build their own services, while DeepSeek still retains high-value businesses such as natively optimized upper-layer services, enterprise privatization consulting, and customized fine-tuning. It no longer only earns the price difference by selling Token APIs, but turns to expand the commercial contact surface of the entire technology stack relying on the ecological scale.

Putting these two histories together, we can get a simple but critical judgment: when enterprises choose open source, it is usually not because open source itself is the goal, but because in a specific competitive position, it is the most effective lever to expand the ecosystem, share costs, and fight against incumbent monopolists. When this competitive position changes, the boundary and sincerity of open source will also change accordingly.

Moreover, the changes at the geopolitical level have further amplified the strategic value of open source. Domestic AI manufacturers are facing the external environment of limited supply of high-end chips, and they do not have natural advantages when simply competing for the training computing power of super-large clusters. Open source has become a differentiated breakthrough path: release models, operators, and inference frameworks to the global community, rely on the optimization of the algorithm layer and scheduling layer to build competitive models under limited computing power conditions, and use the developer community to spontaneously complete adaptation, fine-tuning, and scenario implementation, so that millions of developers around the world can jointly complete ecological construction, without the need for enterprises to invest huge market budgets alone to educate customers.

As for NVIDIA's support for open source, its essence is to prevent the global open source ecosystem from accelerating away from NVIDIA's hardware system and damaging its own hardware business. In this game, open source is no longer just a product strategy, but also a geopolitical chip for computing power manufacturers and model manufacturers to compete for ecological standards.

## 02

However, under the boom, a cruel question hangs over all open source players: open source does not equal victory. Opening weights and underlying codes only means getting the a

# 2026 年阿里云双 11，通义千问 Qwen3.8-Max 详解，多模态能力、智能体任务、代码调用教程

2026-10-26 9

举报

+关注

简介： 对于企业研发团队和专业开发者，当业务需要处理复杂长文档、多步骤科研与金融任务、大型代码项目、多模态专业资料分析时，Qwen3.8-Max是旗舰级的模型选择。落地过程中，做好模型选型区分、提示词调优、上下文缓存配置、密钥安全管理，并且针对高风险业务增加人工复核与结果校验机制，就可以充分发挥模型强大的推理能力，搭建稳定可靠的企业级AI应用与智能体系统。随着模型持续迭代，Qwen3.8-Max的工具调用稳定性、长周期任务规划能力还会持续优化，持续拓展AI在专业领域的落地边界。

在复杂专业任务、长周期智能体、百万字文档精读、多模态深度推理等场景，普通大模型常常出现逻辑断层、长距离信息遗忘、复杂推理精度不足的问题。通义千问Qwen3.8-Max作为Qwen系列旗舰基座大模型，专为高复杂度专业任务打造，总参数量达到2.4万亿，推理时动态激活仅950亿参数，兼顾顶尖推理能力与可控的推理开销。

模型原生支持百万Token超长上下文窗口，原生集成多模态理解、函数调用、联网检索、代码沙盒执行、上下文缓存等全套能力，在文本推理、视觉理解、复杂代码工程、金融量化、法律文书分析等专业基准测试中取得优异成绩。开发者可以通过百炼平台API快速调用，也可依托开源权重做私有化部署，适配企业级智能体、科研数据分析、合同批量审核、大型代码库重构等高要求业务场景。本文将从模型核心功能、底层技术架构、性能特点、API代码实战、业务场景选型、调优策略、开发避坑要点完整展开讲解，帮助开发者全面掌握Qwen3.8-Max的能力边界与落地方法。

## 一、Qwen3.8-Max核心功能介绍

Qwen3.8-Max属于多模态MoE旗舰基础模型，输入支持文本、图片、视频帧，输出为结构化文本内容。百万Token上下文窗口是它的核心亮点，可以一次性加载完整的长篇合同、数百页科研论文、完整项目代码仓库，无需对文档做切片拆分，规避文档分段带来的信息丢失、上下文割裂问题，适合一次性完成全文档的逻辑梳理、交叉校验、摘要提取。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

复杂推理与专业领域能力是Qwen3.8-Max的核心优势。模型针对法律、金融量化、科研、工程开发、设计等专业场景深度优化，能够完成多步骤长周期任务，例如量化研究中并行挖掘多组因子、回测验证、策略迭代；法律场景下批量审阅合同条款，识别风险点，比对多版本合同差异；科研场景阅读大量文献，完成实验方案设计、数据结论校验。在长周期任务中，模型可以自主拆解目标，生成多步骤执行计划，持续迭代反馈，维持长时间任务目标不丢失，这一点在复杂Agent智能体项目中尤为关键。

编程工程能力大幅升级，不再局限于单段代码编写。模型能够读懂完整的多文件项目仓库结构，理解模块之间的依赖关系，完成大型项目重构、漏洞扫描、单元测试编写、多语言工程迁移。面对大型工程需求，能够自主拆分开发任务，生成项目目录结构，分批输出代码文件，同时附带注释、部署文档和排错方案，适配后端、前端、数据分析、量化脚本等各类开发场景，可直接接入各类AI编程开发工具作为底层推理基座。

原生多模态理解能力，支持图片、图表、公式、长视频内容解析。可以识别截图代码、复杂财务报表、工程图纸、数学公式，完成图文混合文档的综合推理；长视频内容可通过抽取关键帧送入模型，完成视频内容摘要、关键事件提取、图表数据读取，在财报分析、试卷批改、科研图表解读场景实用性极强。

内置全套工具调用体系，支持Function Calling自定义工具，同时自带联网搜索、网页内容提取、代码解释器等内置工具。模型会自主判断任务是否需要调用外部工具，自动规划工具调用顺序，执行多轮工具迭代，完成复杂闭环任务。例如，联网检索最新行业资料，调用代码解释器执行数据计算与可视化，抓取网页原文做内容精读，工具调用过程稳定，多工具连续调用时不容易出现逻辑错乱。

同时模型支持结构化输出、上下文缓存、前缀续写、批量推理等实用能力。结构化输出可以强制返回标准JSON格式，大幅降低业务侧解析失败概率；上下文缓存机制针对重复前缀内容做缓存，减少重复Token计算，降低长文档循环调用场景的延迟与计费开销；前缀续写支持从指定文本位置继续生成，适合代码补全、文档续写场景。接口层面兼容OpenAI协议，原有基于OpenAI协议开发的业务系统，仅需要修改模型名称与API地址，少量改动代码即可完成迁移，降低项目改造工作量。

## 二、Qwen3.8-Max技术架构解析

Qwen3.8-Max基于Qwen3.5架构迭代升级，采用稀疏混合专家MoE架构搭配自研混合注意力机制，解决超大参数量模型推理成本高、超长上下文算力爆炸两大痛点。模型总参数规模2.4万亿，但内置路由控制器，收到用户输入之后，路由模块会根据输入文本语义，动态选择少量相关专家网络参与推理，单次推理仅激活950亿参数，其余专家保持休眠状态。这种设计，让模型拥有超大知识库与复杂推理能力，同时推理算力开销远低于同等规模稠密大模型，实现强推理能力与可控推理成本的平衡。

混合注意力机制是支撑百万上下文的底层核心。架构融合多种注意力模块，针对长序列做了针对性优化。对于大量重复、背景类文本，使用线性注意力快速处理，降低算力开销；对于关键信息、需要精细比对的核心段落，切换到高精度稀疏注意力，精准捕捉远距离Token之间的关联关系。百万Token输入场景下，模型不会像传统全注意力模型那样产生平方级算力增长，大幅降低超长文档的预填充耗时，同时保障远距离信息召回精度，避免长篇文档后半段内容遗忘的问题。

模型整体架构分为五层：多模态编码层、词嵌入层、MoE混合专家主干网络层、混合注意力模块、输出预测头。多模态编码层负责将图片、视频帧转为文本对齐的向量表征，和文本向量合并送入主干网络；词嵌入层对文本Token做向量化处理；主干网络由大量专家模块和路由控制器组成，路由动态选择专家参与计算；混合注意力模块在每一层网络内完成序列信息建模；最后输出预测头生成下一个Token。

上下文缓存模块是独立配套优化模块，在多次请求包含相同前缀上下文的场景下，服务端缓存前缀向量，后续请求直接复用缓存结果，不需要重复计算前缀Token。典型场景：反复针对同一篇长文档提问，文档内容作为固定前缀，多次提问只需要计算新问题部分，显著降低Token消耗与接口响应耗时，在知识库问答、批量文档审核场景收益巨大。

训练阶段采用多任务联合训练方案，融合海量专业文本、代码、图文、视频数据，搭配多阶段奖励优化，强化长周期任务规划、多轮工具调用、复杂逻辑推理能力。模型内置多轮任务反馈闭环机制，在Agent任务执行过程中，可以评估当前结果是否满足目标，如果存在偏差，自动调整执行策略，重新规划工具调用步骤，提升长周期复杂任务的成功率。

整套架构同时兼顾云端API调用与私有化本地部署两种模式。云端百炼平台对模型做了分布式负载均衡，自动调度算力资源，高峰期保障接口稳定性；本地部署时，MoE架构支持张量并行，将专家网络拆分到多张GPU卡，合理分配显存开销，在多卡服务器环境下可以实现稳定本地推理。

## 三、Qwen3.8-Max实战接入指南

开发者接入Qwen3.8-Max主要分为两种方式：百炼平台云端API调用，私有化本地部署。云端API无需准备高性能显卡，开箱即用，适合快速原型开发、线上业务落地；本地私有化部署适合数据不允许出网、高数据安全要求的企业场景，需要多卡GPU硬件支撑。下面提供环境配置、curl命令、Python完整可运行代码示例。

第一步，登录百炼平台控制台，创建API密钥，保存DASHSCOPE_API_KEY，密钥妥善保管，禁止硬编码写入代码仓库、前端页面。模型调用标识：qwen3.8-max。
第二步，配置环境变量，Linux/Mac终端执行下面命令：
export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY="sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"

## 四、业务场景选型与模型调优策略

Qwen3.8-Max定位旗舰推理模型，适合对推理精度、长距离逻辑、多步骤任务规划要求高的场景。第一类，专业文档深度分析：法律合同审阅、财报解读、长篇论文精读，一次性加载几十万字文档，完成条款比对、风险识别、结论归纳。第二类，复杂Agent智能体开发，长周期多步骤业务自动化，例如科研辅助、量化研究流水线、多步骤办公自动化，依靠多轮工具调用完成闭环任务。第三类，大型代码工程项目开发，读取完整代码仓库，做代码审计、系统架构重构、漏洞排查、生成全套项目文档。第四类，多模态专业分析，包含图表、公式、截图的混合文档解析，财务报表、工程图纸、科研图表信息提取与推理。

调优策略：专业推理场景，建议调低temperature至0.4~0.6区间，降低随机性，保证推理结果稳定可靠；创意生成类任务可适当调高temperature。长文档场景优先开启上下文缓存，重复文档前缀复用缓存，节省Token开销。如果需要稳定JSON输出，开启结构化输出参数，强制模型返回标准JSON，减少业务侧解析异常。在Agent任务中，设置单次工具调用最大轮次，防止模型无限循环调用工具。

成本优化思路：区分模型选型，简单问答、短文本分类任务不需要使用Qwen3.8-Max，可以选用轻量化模型降低成本；只有复杂推理、长文档、多步骤Agent任务，才使用该旗舰模型。批量任务尽量复用上下文缓存，减少重复Token计费。测试环境和生产环境分开，原型调试阶段使用小批量样本验证提示词逻辑，上线前做压力测试，预估峰值Token消耗。

## 五、开发常见问题与避坑指南

- 百万上下文不是无限制稳定。虽然模型支持百万Token上下文，但上下文越长，接口延迟越高，Token消耗也会显著增加。业务开发时尽量精简输入内容，剔除无效冗余文本，不要无限制堆叠全部历史对话。关键指令尽量放在提示词靠前位置，提升模型对核心要求的关注度。
- MoE路由负载问题。MoE模型依靠路由选择专家，当输入内容高度集中在某一类专业领域，会出现部分专家负载偏高。云端API平台已经做好负载均衡；本地多卡部署时，需要合理设置张量并行，均衡各卡专家负载，避免单卡显存瓶颈。
- 多模态输入限制。图片、视频帧输入会折算为Token占用上下文窗口，一次性传入大量图片会快速消耗上下文额度，多图文任务需要控制单次传入图片数量。
- 密钥安全管控。API密钥禁止写死在前端、客户端代码中，线上业务请求必须经过后端服务中转。生产环境使用环境变量或者密钥管理服务保存密钥，定期轮换密钥，防止密钥泄露造成额度异常消耗。
- 模型输出不能直接用于高风险业务。模型推理存在概率性误差，金融、法律、医疗等高风险场景，模型输出仅作为辅助参考，必须增加人工复核流程，不能直接依靠模型结果自动执行业务操作。
- 结构化输出仍需要做参数校验。即使开启结构化输出能力，代码依然要增加JSON解析异常捕获与字段校验，防止极端场景下输出格式异常，保障业务系统健壮性。

## 六、总结

Qwen3.8-Max作为旗舰级多模态MoE大模型，依托2.4万亿总参数、动态激活950亿专家参数、百万Token超长上下文、混合注意力架构，在复杂专业推理、长周期Agent任务、大型代码工程、多模态深度理解等场景实现能力突破。模型内置联网检索、代码沙盒、网页提取等全套工具能力，兼容主流API协议，支持上下文缓存、结构化输出等企业级能力，开发者既可以快速调用云端API，也可以私有化本地部署。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

对于企业研发团队和专业开发者，当业务需要处理复杂长文档、多步骤科研与金融任务、大型代码项目、多模态专业资料分析时，Qwen3.8-Max是旗舰级的模型选择。落地过程中，做好模型选型区分、提示词调优、上下文缓存配置、密钥安全管理，并且针对高风险业务增加人工复核与结果校验机制，就可以充分发挥模型强大的推理能力，搭建稳定可靠的企业级AI应用与智能体系统。随着模型持续迭代，Qwen3.8-Max的工具调用稳定性、长周期任务规划能力还会持续优化，持续拓展AI在专业领域的落地边界。

## 一、Qwen3.8-Flash核心功能介绍

Qwen3.8-Flash属于MoE混合专家架构模型，总参数量庞大，但每次推理仅激活少量专家参数，兼顾模型能力与推理效率，是兼顾性能与成本的轻量化旗舰模型。模型最核心的亮点是原生支持百万Token超长上下文窗口，借助自研混合稀疏注意力机制，处理几十万甚至百万字文档、完整代码仓库、多轮超长对话时，预填充速度相比传统稠密大模型提升数倍，长文档场景下的成本优势尤为突出。

在编程开发能力方面，Qwen3.8-Flash在SWE-bench Pro、DeepSWE等代码基准测试中取得亮眼成绩，不仅能够独立完成单段代码编写、Bug修复、代码注释生成，还支持理解完整项目仓库结构，自主规划多文件工程开发，迭代调试复杂项目逻辑，适配后端服务、前端页面、脚本工具等多语言开发场景，能够直接对接Claude Code、Cursor、Qoder CN等编程开发工具，作为代码底层推理模型使用。

Agent工具调用是该模型重点强化的能力，在Toolathlon、CoWorkBench等智能体基准测试中表现优异，支持多轮自主规划、工具选择、结果校验、迭代修正。模型可以自主调用联网检索、代码沙盒执行、文档解析等工具，完成复杂长周期任务，例如批量解析PDF合同、自动处理多步骤办公流程、完成多轮数据计算与结果校验，数千轮连续交互过程中能够维持稳定的任务闭环，不容易出现任务遗忘、逻辑跑偏等问题。

原生多模态能力也是Qwen3.8-Flash的核心特性，支持图片、图表、公式、长视频内容理解。可以读取截图内代码、识别表格数据、解析数学公式，完成图文混合文档分析；长视频理解能力支持读取视频帧信息，完成视频内容摘要、关键信息提取，在教育、科研、金融财报分析、图纸解析场景具备很高实用价值。

## 二、Qwen3.8-Flash技术架构解析

Qwen3.8-Flash采用全新一代模型架构，在注意力机制、残差信息流、词嵌入、优化器四个维度完成系统性升级，整套架构由GDN门控线性注意力、QSA稀疏注意力、四分支门控残差、N-gram嵌入查表模块共同组成，解决传统Transformer在超长上下文场景算力开销大、信息丢失、训练不稳定的问题。

第一，GDN+QSA混合稀疏注意力机制。模型每四层网络设置组合结构，三层使用Gated DeltaNet（GDN）门控线性注意力，一层使用自研QSA（Qwen Sparse Attention）稀疏注意力。GDN擅长处理长序列，算力开销不会随着文本长度呈平方级增长；QSA负责检索关键信息，对上下文做微块粒度索引，精准召回关键内容。二者结合之后，百万上下文场景下，文档预填充速度提升7倍以上，同时保证长文本远端信息召回准确率，解决传统全量注意力在百万上下文场景算力爆炸的难题。传统稠密模型读取百万字文档，需要巨大算力完成全部Token之间的相关性计算，而Qwen3.8-Flash依靠混合稀疏注意力，只对关键信息做高精度注意力计算，其余序列使用线性注意力快速处理，大幅降低算力消耗。

第二，四分支Gated Residual门控残差结构。传统Transformer只有单条残差信息流，多层叠加之后容易出现特征稀释、关键信息被后续层覆盖的问题。Qwen3.8-Flash将信息流拆分为四条独立并行通道，通过门控机制动态控制每一条通道的读写权限。核心特征可以保留在独立通道不被污染，次要特征在其他通道并行更新，信息传递效率更高，深度网络训练过程更加稳定，在超长多轮Agent任务中，能够长时间保留初始任务目标，不容易遗忘前置指令。

第三，N-gram Embedding词块查表模块。模型额外附带51B规模的N-gram嵌入查表参数，这部分参数不会参与每一步Token推理计算，几乎不增加推理算力开销，相当于外挂一个大规模语义记忆库。模型在推理阶段可以直接查表召回高频固定词块、专业术语、固定搭配的语义向量，不需要实时计算组合语义，大幅降低长文本输入阶段的计算量，对于专业文档、代码文本、行业术语密集场景，加速效果非常明显。

第四，Muon优化器协同优化。模型训练阶段采用Muon优化器，配合全新架构协同调优，提升训练收敛速度与训练吞吐，让模型在海量多模态、代码、Agent任务数据上学习效率更高，模型权重分布更稳定，推理阶段输出一致性更好。

整体架构采用MoE混合专家设计，全部专家参数存储在模型内部，当输入一段提示词，路由模块会根据输入内容，只激活最相关的少量专家参数参与推理，其余专家保持休眠状态。这种设计实现“大模型能力，小模型推理成本”，兼顾复杂任务的理解能力与普通任务的推理速度。

整套架构分为输入层、混合注意力层、门控残差网络层、N-gram查表模块、输出预测头。输入文本、图片多模态数据，经过向量化处理送入网络；N-gram模块预取词块向量；混合注意力模块完成序列信息建模；四分支残差通道传递特征；最后预测头输出下一个Token，多模态任务额外接入视觉编码分支，将图片、视频帧转为向量，和文本向量融合进入主干网络。

## 四、业务场景选型与性能优化策略

Qwen3.8-Flash的能力特性决定了它在几类场景具备突出优势。第一类是长文档处理场景，合同解析、论文精读、知识库百万字资料问答，百万上下文窗口可以一次性加载完整文档，不需要做文档切片、分段摘要，减少切片带来的信息断裂问题。第二类是代码工程开发，读取完整代码仓库，做代码重构、漏洞检测、项目文档生成，接入代码编辑器作为AI编程助手。第三类是多轮Agent智能体，自动化办公、数据处理流水线、多步骤业务审批机器人，依靠稳定工具调用能力完成复杂任务。第四类多模态图文分析，财报图表识别、试卷公式计算、图纸文字提取、长视频摘要。

业务调优技巧：处理长文档时，适当调低temperature参数，降低随机性，保证提取信息准确；简单问答任务可以设置较低max_tokens，减少不必要Token消耗；批量离线任务建议关闭流式输出，减少网络请求开销；Agent场景，限制单次工具调用数量，增加结果校验逻辑，防止模型无限循环调用工具。

成本优化：长文档优先利用Qwen3.8-Flash长上下文加速优势，相比普通大模型，同等文档处理任务Token消耗更低；区分测试环境和生产环境，测试阶段使用小批量样本调试提示词，上线前做压力测试，预估峰值Token消耗。

## 五、开发常见问题与避坑指南

- 长上下文并非无限稳定。虽然支持百万Token上下文，但上下文越长，推理耗时越高，成本随之上升。业务设计时尽量精简输入上下文，过滤无效冗余文本，不要无限制塞入全部历史对话。高关键信息召回场景，建议在提示词开头放置核心指令，提升模型对核心要求的关注度。
- MoE模型推理存在路由逻辑。当输入内容偏向特定领域，路由会固定激活部分专家，极端场景下个别专家负载偏高，云端API平台已经做负载均衡，本地部署需要做好多卡张量并行，均衡专家负载。
- 多模态输入限制。图片、视频输入会占用上下文Token额度，图片会转为向量编码折算为对应Token，大量图片同时输入会快速消耗上下文窗口，多图文任务需要控制单次传入图片数量。
- 密钥安全管理。API密钥禁止直接写死在前端页面、客户端代码，所有请求必须经过后端服务中转；生产环境使用环境变量或者密钥管理服务存储密钥，定期轮换密钥，防止泄露造成额度消耗。
- 工具调用的边界。模型会自主判断何时调用工具，但无法保证100%判断准确。高风险业务，资金、风控类场景，必须增加人工复核环节，不能完全依赖模型输出自动执行业务操作。
- 量化本地部署损失。使用低比特量化版本本地部署，会小幅降低代码、复杂推理能力，对精度要求高的项目，优先使用完整权重部署。

## 六、总结

Qwen3.8-Flash依靠GDN+QSA混合稀疏注意力、四分支门控残差、N-gram查表嵌入等创新架构，突破传统大模型长上下文算力瓶颈，在百万级长文档、代码工程、多轮Agent智能体、多模态图文理解场景实现速度、成本、效果三者平衡。模型同时提供云端API调用与开源本地部署两条路径，兼容主流API协议，开发者可以快速迁移现有项目，降低改造工作量。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

对于独立开发者和企业研发团队来说，如果业务需要处理超长文档、搭建代码助手、开发自动化智能体，Qwen3.8-Flash是性价比很高的选型。在落地过程中，合理规划上下文长度、做好提示词调优、设置工具调用校验逻辑，同时做好密钥安全管控，就能充分发挥模型架构带来的速度与成本优势，稳定支撑AI应用的线上业务运行。随着后续版本迭代，Qwen3.8-Flash的工具调用稳定性、多模态理解能力还会持续优化，会成为各类AI智能体与长文本应用的核心底层模型。

简介： Qwen3‑VL‑Plus不是一款"更强的识图工具"，而是一个从感知到决策、从分析到执行的完整视觉智能体基座。它以原生多模态融合打破感知壁垒，以256K超长上下文突破信息边界，以思考模式混合设计兼顾深度与速度，以百炼平台的全链路生态让落地门槛降至最低。对于开发者，几行代码即可接入；对于企业，可视化智能体编排无需深度编码；对于行业，法务、财务、产品、媒体、教育……每一个需要"看懂画面"的场景，都能找到它的用武之地。现在就前往阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面，领取免费Tokens，开启你的视觉智能体实战之旅。

当大模型从"纸上谈兵"迈向"实战落地"，视觉智能已不再是锦上添花的点缀，而是决定AI能否真正"看懂世界"的命脉。通义千问Qwen3‑VL‑Plus，正是通义千问Qwen3系列中那柄最锋利的视觉利刃——它原生融合文本、图片、视频三大输入模态，以262144 token的超长上下文窗口与OSWorld权威测试中的行业顶尖水准，宣告了视觉语言模型从"看图说话"到"理解业务逻辑"的质变。本文将从架构底层、核心能力、API实操到行业落地，逐层拆解这款旗舰模型的全部价值，更多详情可前往 阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

## 一、模型定位：为什么是Qwen3‑VL‑Plus？

Qwen3‑VL‑Plus并非简单的"文本模型+视觉插件"拼凑产物，而是通义千问Qwen3系列的旗舰视觉‑语言基座模型。它采用思考模式与非思考模式混合融合设计，无需切换模型即可兼顾复杂多步推理与简单场景快速响应——这意味着开发者不必在"深度分析"和"极速应答"之间左右为难，一套模型吃透全场景。更多模型选型与能力对比，请前往 阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 查阅。

从产品矩阵来看，Qwen3‑VL‑Plus在通义千问家族中占据独特生态位：

模型层级 | 代表型号 | 核心定位 
---|---|---
旗舰推理 | Qwen3.8‑Max‑Preview | 全链路智能体执行、深度逻辑推理 
均衡通用 | Qwen3‑Plus / Qwen3‑Flash | 性价比主力、高并发场景 
视觉旗舰 | Qwen3‑VL‑Plus | 文本+图片+视频原生融合、复杂视觉推理 
超长文本 | Qwen‑Long | 千万级Token、整本书/全套合同分析 
代码专项 | Qwen3‑Coder | 全栈代码生成与调试 
音频专项 | Qwen‑Audio‑3.0 | 语音识别与情感化合成 

Qwen3‑VL‑Plus的独特价值在于：它是唯一同时具备"视觉编码深度优化+跨模态对齐+长序列处理"三重能力的视觉语言模型，能够胜任文档数字化、视觉智能体自动化、前端开发辅助、媒体内容分析、图纸报表解析等大量专业业务。更多模型能力详情可访问 阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面。

## 二、四大核心技术突破：从底层架构看竞争力

### 1. 原生多模态早期融合，告别"拼接式"视觉

传统视觉语言模型往往采用"文本编码器+视觉编码器后期对齐"的拼接思路，导致图表、截图、视频等复杂视觉内容的理解精度大打折扣。Qwen3‑VL‑Plus采用Token级早期融合训练，图像、视频、音频信号与文本统一编码——不是后期拼接，而是从底层就"长在一起"。这种架构带来的直接收益是：对倾斜文档、模糊扫描件、带水印图片的OCR识别依然稳定，中文混合语种OCR表现尤为突出。技术细节与评测数据可在 阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 获取。

### 2. 256K Token多模态上下文，跨图跨页关联分析

传统视觉模型输入大量图片或长视频帧后，极易出现"细节遗忘、表格错乱、跨图逻辑断裂"的顽疾，开发者不得不人为拆分素材分批提交，业务复杂度陡增。Qwen3‑VL‑Plus原生支持256K token多模态上下文窗口，可同时承载大段文本资料、多张扫描文档截图、报表图片、长视频解析帧序列与字幕文本，一次性完成跨图片、跨页面的关联对比分析。依托优化后的跨模态编码器与序列处理机制，信息召回稳定性显著提升。更多能力演示可前往 阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 体验。

### 3. 上下文缓存机制，智能体工作流的"降本利器"

在智能体多轮对话场景中，系统提示词、固定业务规则、公共参考素材属于大量请求复用的静态前缀内容。Qwen3‑VL‑Plus原生支持上下文缓存机制：静态部分只执行一次预填充运算，后续多轮对话直接复用缓存结果，不再重复计算图像与文本特征。这不仅有效减少token消耗，更大幅降低接口响应延迟，尤其适合长时间不间断运行的视觉自动化工作流服务。缓存配置与优化策略详见 阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面。

### 4. 思考模式+非思考模式混合，推理深度随心切换

每一个Qwen3系列模型都支持思考模式开关。开启后，模型生成内部推理过程，消耗更多Token但输出更严谨；非思考模式输出简洁、速度更快。Qwen3‑VL‑Plus将二者混合融合，不需要切换模型就可以兼顾复杂多步推理与简单场景快速响应——这在实际业务中意味着：同一套API调用，既能处理需要深度分析的法务合同审查，也能胜任高并发的简单图片分类任务。具体模式切换方法可参考 阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面。

# 非洲、东南亚、欧美企业都在用中国AI｜经观中国

人工智能（AI）浪潮席卷各行各业，但并非所有国家都能立即享受技术发展带来的红利。

在东南亚地区，语言多达1200余种，民众日常交流中普遍存在多种语言混用的复杂情况。可西方主流AI大模型的预训练数据中，80%以上是标准英语，东南亚语言内容占比一度只有0.5%。这导致不少标准的“美式”AI大模型在东南亚出现“水土不服”。

中国民营企业开发的AI大模型奔赴海外。

在东南亚，阿里巴巴通义千问等民企AI大模型在预训练阶段就已涵盖当地上百种语言，为理解东南亚小语种打下基础。

无独有偶，非洲国家在同步测试美国和中国民企AI大模型时，也发现中国AI大模型表现更优、成本更低，且开源模型让不少国家可利用自己的数据实现“定制化”服务，服务本土民众。在欧美地区，跨国企业也纷纷将中国AI大模型视为“降本增效”的“香饽饽”。

中国民企前沿AI大模型正在全球掀起一股“中国风”。

中国AI大模型，正在全球“霸榜”

全球AI大模型的竞争格局正在迎来新一轮洗牌。此前，全球AI大模型多由西方科技巨头主导，如今这一局面正逐渐被打破，中国民企研发的多款AI大模型，日趋走向世界舞台的聚光灯下。

从深度求索（DeepSeek）到阿里巴巴的通义千问；从月之暗面的Kimi K3到MiniMax的M3、腾讯的混元Hy4 preview；从智谱的GLM、阶跃星辰的Step 5 Preview，到字节跳动的豆包、百度的文心一言……中国多个民企AI大模型集群式崛起，在全球强势“出圈”。

中国民企研发的AI大模型不仅凭借稳定的技术输出、高性价比，在全球赢得越来越多的用户青睐与认可，更凭借开源的技术生态，让创新技术红利普惠全球，加速重构全球AI产业版图。

行业数据印证了这一重要趋势。全球AI模型聚合平台OpenRouter统计，2026年以来，中国AI大模型周调用量稳居全球前列，来自中国的多个头部模型更长期“霸榜”词元（Token）调用量榜单前排。

据OpenRouter最新数据测算，上周（10月5日至10月11日）全球AI大模型总调用量为172万亿Token。其中，上榜的AI大模型中，中国AI大模型周调用量达86.74万亿Token， 是同期美国（18.97万亿Token）的4.5倍。同期，全球调用量排名前五均为中国AI大模型。

Token调用量是衡量AI大模型真实使用强度与应用广度的核心指标——每一次调用，都对应着一次真实场景的交互，从企业智能客服到开发者代码生成，从日常文案创作到复杂数据分析，Token的消耗直接折射出AI在千行百业的渗透深度。

从趋势看，中国AI大模型总调用量在全球保持领先优势。据OpenRouter统计，截至10月11日，中国大模型周调用量连续二十四周超过美国，稳居全球首位。

中国AI大模型何以“出圈”？

中国AI大模型之所以被全球用户高频选择，核心在于其具有高性价比。

从价格上看，OpenRouter 负责数据与分析工作的贾斯汀·萨默维尔（Justin Summerville）在接受美国消费者新闻与商业频道（CNBC）采访时透露，中国开源大模型的价格相较Anthropic、OpenAI的头部模型普遍低60%至90%。

美国研究公司Artificial Analysis的官网数据给出了更直观的对比。

从中美AI大模型阵营里定价价位较高的代表来看，截至10月17日，中国月之暗面的Kimi K3每百万Token输入价格为3美元、输出价格为15美元，平均每项任务成本达2美元；而美国Anthropic的Claude Fable 5.1输入价格为10美元、输出价格为50美元，平均每项任务成本达7.63美元。

总体看，Claude Fable 5.1的输入、输出价格均为Kimi K3的3.3倍，单任务成本更是达到3.8倍——这意味着，花同样的钱，用Kimi K3能跑近4个任务。Claude Fable 5.1输入价格和输出价格均是DeepSeek V4.1 Flash的数十倍，平均每项成本是DeepSeek V4.1 Flash的28倍。

高性能，也是中国AI大模型受欢迎的关键。随着中国AI大模型性能不断提升，中美在AI赛道已从“追赶”进入“局部并跑甚至反超”阶段。

美国斯坦福大学今年发布的《2026年AI指数报告》显示，自2025年初以来，中美两国模型已多次交替登顶性能榜单。过去一年来，这一差距虽有波动，但始终保持在个位数。截至2026年3月，美国顶尖模型和中国顶尖模型之间的差距仅有2.7%。

中国AI大模型性能的提升，也引起海外科技圈人士的密切关注。

美国芯片巨头英特尔首席执行官陈立武近日表示，DeepSeek、Kimi和GLM等中国前沿AI模型不仅使用成本较低，而且性能已经“足够好”，能够满足实际应用需求，市场采用速度也“非常快”。

英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋曾多次公开称赞中国开源AI模型“非常优秀”，其降低了AI的使用门槛，将扩大整体市场规模，拉动芯片和数据中心需求。

特斯拉CEO埃隆·马斯克近期在接受中国媒体采访时也认为中国AI模型进步速度令人惊叹，单位算力产出的性能近乎全球顶尖水平。他并表示中国AI公司在未来某个节点成为领跑者的概率相当高。

业界人士分析，中国AI大模型能兼顾性能与成本，核心在于两方面协同发力。一方面，得益于技术路线创新，算力消耗和推理成本大幅降低；另一方面，稳定的能源供给与完善的算力基础设施，进一步压低单位算力成本。

二者叠加，不仅让技术不断升级、成本持续下降、应用快速铺开，形成正向循环，也让中国大模型在性价比上更有优势。

中国开源模型正在重构世界AI版图

“中国的开源AI是推动全球进步的催化剂，让各国和各行业都有机会参与这一革命。”黄仁勋此前指出，中国开放的AI大模型，降低了AI的使用门槛，推动全球AI快速发展。

在东南亚，中国AI大模型通过本地化语言适配，解决了西方以英文为主的通用语言模型在东南亚市场“水土不服”的痛点——从新加坡国家级“海狮”模型全面转向阿里通义千问基座，到马来西亚政府服务能力建设，中国模型正在用更贴合本地需求的方案，填补西方模型在多语种、低算力场景下的能力空白。

在欧美，中国AI大模型正成为企业降本和初创公司融资的“双重助手”。

据英国《金融时报》报道，为降低技术成本，美国外卖巨头DoorDash、全球旅行房屋租赁平台爱彼迎和德国科技巨头西门子等大型企业纷纷转向中国人工智能模型。另据美国投资机构数据，目前多达80%的美国AI初创公司在融资路演时，会使用中国的开源模型。

在肯尼亚、尼日利亚等非洲国家，越来越多的开发者正把中国开源模型变成本地创新的“工具箱”：有人用它优化商业服务流程，有人为高中生开发教育工具，还有人搭建面向本地用户的聊天机器人……

在影视行业，中国AI大模型也大施拳脚。美国流媒体平台亚马逊热播剧《大卫王朝》第一季，共包含72个运用AI技术的镜头，其中视频生成部分由国产视频生成大模型代表可灵AI参与。主创表示，AI 技术让制作团队在几周内完成原本需要4至5个月的工作量，同时还大量节约制作成本。

中国信息通信研究院云计算与数字化研究所副所长栗蔚指出，现在全球更多的、各行各业的人，都在基于中国的大模型进行再次开发，从而反哺和激发出一批新技术和新应用，极大提升了AI融入各行各业实际应用的速度。

美媒CNBC近期刊文指出，尽管美国在代码编程、智能体等高阶能力上仍保持领先，但随着中国AI模型性能快速追赶，叠加可下载、可修改、可本地部署的开源生态优势，中国AI大模型正越来越可能成为全球尤其是发展中国家的“默认选择”。

当顶尖的AI能力不再被锁在少数巨头的围墙里，当全球每一个开发者都能以极低的成本调用甚至自主部署这些模型，中国开源AI大模型带给世界的，就不仅仅是一项技术——而是一场推动各国平等共享新一轮科技革命红利的深刻变革。

GLM.title: Tang Jie Signed Paper Unveils Zhipu AI’s In-House Multimodal Model: Is Next-Gen GLM Nearing Launch?
GLM.description: In August this year, Zhipu AI launched GLM-5.3-Flash, calling it the first native multimodal model in the GLM-5 series. ... The model GLM-Omni is based on Zhipu AI's open-source GLM-4.1V-Thinking with a parameter size of 9B...
GLM.content:
# Tang Jie's signed paper reveals the in-house multimodal model, is the next-generation GLM on the horizon?

AI前线2026-10-26 07:55

Zhipu GLM-Omni explores visual generation to empower language reasoning

After the stunning debut of GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash (the two models belong to the same series in name but are trained with different base models), Zhipu AI has continuously improved the model's capabilities in coding, long-term agents and other fields. However, how the next-generation GLM will be upgraded remains a key direction that draws widespread public attention.

Apart from stronger reasoning performance and lower cost, another noteworthy direction is: native multimodality.

Recently, researchers from Tsinghua University and Zhipu AI jointly published a paper on arXiv titled 《Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?》, with the corresponding author being Tang Jie, Chief Scientist of Zhipu AI and Professor of Tsinghua University.

The paper introduces GLM-Omni, an undisclosed internal model of Zhipu AI, and attempts to answer a somewhat counterintuitive question: Can the knowledge the model learns through image generation be transformed into language reasoning capabilities?

In the experiment, GLM-Omni achieved a 72% success rate in correctly drawing the specified jersey number on digital tasks, but if no image was provided and the same number was only asked in text, the accuracy rate was only 2%.

The researchers then adjusted the training method, allowing the model to put image generation, image observation and text answers into the same training sequence. The average text question-answering accuracy of the model increased from 12.57% to 26.86%. On this basis, when the model was allowed to generate an image first and then observe the image to answer the question before responding, the accuracy further increased to 41.14%.

This study is not direct evidence that the next-generation GLM will adopt a certain architecture, but it provides a research and development clue worthy of tracking: After Zhipu AI has realized native multimodal understanding on GLM-5.3-Flash, researchers are still exploring how to establish a closer connection between visual generation and language reasoning.

## Zhipu AI is just missing you

To understand the significance of this paper, we must first clarify a concept: Native multimodality does not mean that the model can generate images on its own.

In August this year, Zhipu AI launched GLM-5.3-Flash, calling it the first native multimodal model in the GLM-5 series. It adopts a brand-new pre-trained base, supports multimodal inputs such as images and videos, can understand the interface and observe rendering results in the Coding Agent workflow, and continue to modify the code according to interactive feedback.

However, from the perspective of the public model interface, the main output of GLM-5.3-Flash is still text. Its ability to understand visual information does not mean that it can natively generate images in the same model.

This is also an important technical demarcation point for current multimodal models.

One type of model mainly focuses on the unified understanding of multiple types of information, enabling the model to simultaneously process inputs including text, images, videos and other content;

The other type of model further attempts to unify understanding and generation, so that the same model can not only understand visual content, but also directly generate images, and explore knowledge sharing between the two capabilities.

The problems faced by the latter are not only how to draw images well, but also whether the knowledge the model learns from generation tasks can be called by other tasks.

When Tang Jie previously talked about native multimodality, his focus was not only on adding an additional input or output capability. In his view, the unified perception of information such as vision, sound and even touch is an important foundation for the model to further understand the environment and perform long-term tasks.

For Agents that need to continuously observe the environment and adjust actions based on feedback, multimodality is not just a function expansion, it also determines whether the model can truly be applied to complex real-world tasks.

In June this year, a netizen asked Musk on X: When will Chinese models reach the level of Fable? Musk replied that it might be in the first quarter. Tang Jie commented: It won't take that long.

On the evening of October 21, the official operation team sent a compensation notice to users of the programming package. At the end of the notice, it was also written: "An additional reset card will be given away after the new model is released", which is equivalent to an announcement that the update is coming soon.

## The Hidden Capabilities of Multimodal Output

Tang Jie, the corresponding author of the paper, is the Chief Scientist of Zhipu AI. The three co-first authors, Li Wenkai, Hong Wenyi and Yang Zhuoyi, completed this research during their internship at Zhipu AI.

The model GLM-Omni is based on Zhipu AI's open-source GLM-4.1V-Thinking with a parameter size of 9B, which is a relatively small test model. The research team proposed a test method called Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP), whose core is to distinguish two things:

Whether the model has learned a certain piece of knowledge during image generation;

Whether it can express this knowledge through language.

This is also a potential value worthy of exploration for unified multimodal models. It can not only allow the model to view and draw images at the same time, but also enable knowledge learned from different modalities to complement each other, rather than working independently.

To verify this, the researchers constructed a fictional world called MagicWorld, where entities such as teams, characters and badges do not exist in reality. For example, a fictional team has the jersey number 10. During training, the model was only taught to generate images of jerseys printed with the number 10, and this number was not provided in the text prompts.

The dataset contains 7 types of knowledge including color, quantity, number, shape, spatial location, with a total of 350 entries, which is expanded into 8552 sets of image training samples. This can largely rule out the possibility that the model answers questions relying on existing text memory.

The participants in the test include not only the internal Zhipu AI GLM-Omni, but also BAGEL from ByteDance and SenseNova-U1 from SenseTime. The three models adopt different visual generation architectures. The researchers respectively checked whether they can correctly draw the target attributes and answer questions in text without the assistance of images.

The first round of experiments immediately revealed the obvious phenomenon of "being able to draw but not being able to describe".

GLM-Omni's average image generation accuracy reached 54%, but the accuracy of directly answering questions about the same knowledge in text was only 14.57%. Among them, the image accuracy rate of digital tasks was 72%, while the text question-answering accuracy rate was only 2%. The gap in digital tasks of SenseNova-U1 was even larger, at 88% and 0% respectively.

This means that the model can already reproduce certain knowledge in the process of image generation, but it is difficult to directly call it through language. In other words, putting visual generation and language understanding into the same model does not mean that the knowledge mastered by the two capabilities can automatically communicate with each other.

So, where exactly is the problem? The researchers then tried two different training methods.

The first method is text alignment: add text question-answering pairs for some fictional entities, let the model learn how to answer related questions, and then test whether it can transfer the learned knowledge to entities that have never seen text answers.

But the effect was not stable. GLM-Omni's average text accuracy even dropped from 14.57% to 12.57%. This shows that simply adding text question-answering pairs is not enough to stably convert visual knowledge into language capabilities.

The second method is more interesting, called Interleaved Image–Text Alignment.

The researchers no longer treat image generation and question answering as two independent tasks, but put them into the same training sequence. For example, when the model faces a question about a jersey number, it first generates the related image, then observes the image, and finally gives the text answer.

As a result, in the text test that did not allow temporary drawing, GLM-Omni's average accuracy increased from 12.57% to 26.86%.

To confirm whether the improvement came from image generation, the researchers also conducted a set of controlled experiments: retaining the same training samples and text supervision, only removing the loss signal of the image generation part in the interleaved training. As a result, the accuracy dropped back to 13.71%.

This reveals the first important conclusion of the paper:

1) The knowledge sharing of the unified model not only depends on whether the architecture is unified, but also depends on whether the training signals of different tasks can be effectively connected.

2) Image generation provides more than just an output function, it itself may help the model build knowledge associations that can be utilized by other tasks.

However, even after joint training, a large amount of visual knowledge of the model still cannot be directly expressed in text. The researchers then changed their thinking: since the model can draw the answer, why not let it draw the relevant content first when answering the question?

This is the Visual Chain-of-Thought adopted in the third round of experiments.

GLM.title: Huawei, DeepSeek AI training linked to pirated books by Korean authors
GLM.description: Chinese AI company Zhipu AI, also known as Z.ai, and Tsinghua University identified The Pile as a training data source for their jointly developed language model GLM in a 2022 technical report. It is also unclear whether Zhipu AI trained its model on all the novels included in The Pile.
GLM.content:
# Huawei, DeepSeek AI training linked to pirated books by Korean authors

Huawei and DeepSeek training data may have included unauthorized works by Han Kang and other Korean authors.

Chinese companies, including Huawei and DeepSeek, were found to have used datasets containing pirated books by Korean authors — including Nobel laureate Han Kang — to train their AI models.

The Pile, a collection of books, academic papers, web documents and other materials compiled for AI training that contains approximately 800 gigabytes of data, was one of the sources of English-language text used to train Huawei's AI model Pangu Sigma, according to JoongAng Ilbo's analysis of the company's technical report published in March 2023 on arXiv, a platform for sharing scientific research papers.

A paper describing the dataset on arXiv confirms that it includes Books3, a collection of pirated e-books that Anthropic also downloaded without authorization. A list of works included in Books3, available on GitHub, shows that the collection contains English translations of at least 19 books by 10 Korean authors.

They include Han Kang's "Human Acts" (2014) and "The Vegetarian" (2007), Hwang Sok-yong's "Princess Bari" (2023), Shin Kyung-sook's "Please Look After Mom" (2008) and Kim Young-ha's "I Have the Right to Destroy Myself" (1996).

However, it remains unclear whether Huawei trained its model on all the novels included in the dataset or only some of them.

The use of Books3 became a central issue in the copyright lawsuit "Bartz v. Anthropic," which Anthropic agreed to settle by paying copyright holders $3,000 per book.

The creators of The Pile explained in the dataset's documentation that digital books were included because they were extremely valuable for research into modeling long contexts and maintaining narrative coherence.

The Pile is one of the datasets frequently used by AI researchers. Chinese AI company Zhipu AI, also known as Z.ai, and Tsinghua University identified The Pile as a training data source for their jointly developed language model GLM in a 2022 technical report. It is also unclear whether Zhipu AI trained its model on all the novels included in The Pile.

### DeepSeek reproduces Han Kang's words

DeepSeek, another major Chinese AI company, has also provided information about the sources of its training data.

The company used 860,000 English-language e-books and 180,000 Chinese-language e-books obtained from Anna's Archive to train its DeepSeek-VL model, according to a technical report published in March 2024. Anna's Archive is a website that provides access to pirated books.

Anna's Archive includes English translations of works by prominent Korean authors such as Han, Hwang and Kim, as well as Chinese translations of books including Kim Ae-ran's "The Luck of Flight" (2012).

However, DeepSeek did not download every book available on the site and instead selected materials for training. It therefore remains unclear whether books by Korean authors were among those it obtained.

Researchers have nevertheless found indirect evidence suggesting that DeepSeek may have trained its models on Korean literary works.

DeepSeek 3.1 produced a sequence of 19 consecutive words matching the original text of Han's "The Vegetarian" after undergoing a process known as fine-tuning, according to a paper by researchers from Columbia University, Carnegie Mellon University and other institutions. The paper was first released in March and updated for a fifth time in September.

The reproduced words are: " […] vegetarian, I'd always thought of her as completely unremarkable in every way. To be frank, the first time […]"

Although the findings have not yet undergone peer review, the researchers interpreted the result as indirect evidence that the AI model had been pretrained on the novel.

Anna's Archive also acknowledged widespread interest from developers in its book collection following the rise of generative AI.

"Virtually all major companies building LLMs contacted us to train on our data," the website said in a blog post published in January last year.

The website added that most U.S. companies, though not all, reconsidered after learning that its operations were illegal.

"By contrast, Chinese firms have enthusiastically embraced our collection, apparently untroubled by its legality," the website wrote.

### Pirated books: An AI industry practice?

The use of pirated e-books to train AI models is not limited to Anthropic and Chinese AI companies. Copyright lawsuits have also revealed that OpenAI and Meta downloaded pirated copies of books without authorization.

"The use of pirated books as AI training data is widely known within the AI industry," said Choo Jae-gul, a professor at KAIST's Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI. "Using publicly available datasets to train AI models was standard practice, and some of those datasets included pirated books. There was a period when the AI industry was so caught up in the race to improve model performance that companies indiscriminately used copyrighted data without seriously considering the legal implications."

Choo explained that training AI models on copyrighted digital books was widespread around the world during the early stages of AI development.

"It was common enough for researchers to disclose publicly available datasets containing pirated books as sources of training data in their papers," Choo said.

"As the issue has increasingly drawn scrutiny in recent years, many major technology companies have begun keeping their training data confidential," he added.

BY YOON SUNG-MIN [lee.taehee2@joongang.co.kr]

GLM.title: Rippling 因使用被列入黑名单的中国AI模型而受到审视 - 今日头条
GLM.description: 5.2 而面临质疑。该模型来自中国AI实验室 Z.ai(又称智谱),该公司已被列入美国政府的贸易黑名单。《每日来电者新闻基金会》(Daily ... 布鲁金斯学会(Brookings)研究员凯尔·陈(Kyle Chan)则称,最大的风险来自直接调用Z.ai的API。
GLM.content:
\# Rippling 因使用被列入黑名单的中国AI模型而受到审视

总部位于旧金山的人力资源软件公司 Rippling 因测试 GLM 5\.2 而面临质疑。该模型来自中国AI实验室 Z\.ai\(又称智谱\)\,该公司已被列入美国政府的贸易黑名单。《每日来电者新闻基金会》\(Daily Caller News Foundation\)周六发布的一篇报道发现\,Rippling 的高层管理人员测试了这一模型\,并公开予以推介。安全分析人士警告称\,中国的AI系统可能会让企业敏感数据面临风险。

\# Rippling 做了什么

7月30日\,Rippling 首席执行官帕克·康拉德\(Parker Conrad\)在 X 上写道\:“这就是开放权重模型如此重要的原因——GLM 5\.2 便宜了 85\%\,性能却几乎不相上下。”在发布这条帖子之前\,公司对开放权重模型和几家大型实验室的模型做了约 2\,100 次评分测试。据 TechCrunch 报道\,基准测试结果显示 Grok 的综合表现最好。随后\,Rippling 搭建了一个 AI 网关\,把每条提示词分配给能胜任该任务的最便宜的模型。在使用量基本持平的情况下\,7月的 token 成本降到了4月的 37\%。

据《每日呼声报》\(Daily Caller\)报道\,Rippling 总裁马特·麦金尼斯\(Matt MacInnis\)公布了7月的测试结果\,称 GLM“似乎为降低成本提供了一条捷径”。该媒体还称\,根据首席技术官阿尔伯特·斯特拉斯海姆\(Albert Strasheim\)的一条 LinkedIn 帖子\,他在8月使用 GLM 5\.2 进行了一次“安全审查”。对于公司在多大程度上依赖中国模型\,以及如何保护客户数据\,Rippling 没有回应相关提问。报道称\,Rippling 的客户包括国防初创公司 Askari Defense 在内\,在美国有超过 2 万家企业。报道还提到\,Rippling 公开发布的 AI 指南把 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 列为主要供应商。每日呼声新闻基金会\(Daily Caller News Foundation\)表示\,自己也是 Rippling 的客户。

\# 黑名单之问

智谱是在2025年1月被列入实体清单的，而不是2026年1月。当月，美国商务部工业与安全局将北京智谱华章科技及其九家关联实体列入清单，理由是它们通过人工智能研究推动\"中国军事现代化\"。路透社当时报道称，智谱回应说这一决定\"缺乏事实依据\"。列入清单后，智谱对美国的出口受到限制，但企业仍可以下载其开源模型。

\# 成本与风险的权衡

美国企业研究所\(American Enterprise Institute\)研究员瑞安·费杜夏克\(Ryan Fedusiak\)对《每日呼声》\(Daily Caller\)表示\,把数据通过位于中国的服务器传输\,会带来\"和TikTok一样的问题\,只不过严重程度放大了100倍\"。布鲁金斯学会\(Brookings\)研究员凯尔·陈\(Kyle Chan\)则称\,最大的风险来自直接调用Z\.ai的API。他说\,通过第三方平台运行该模型\,风险\"小得多\,但并非为零\"。

Rippling并不是个例。很多公司也已采用更便宜的中国模型。费杜夏克说\,对于想节省资金的初创公司\,他\"很难去责怪\"\,但\"风险确实存在\,人们不应该对此视而不见\"。

GLM.content:
# 
Open-Source AI Models Are Catching up to Closed Ones on Accounting Work, DualEntry Benchmark Finds

Share

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro got 86.1% of tasks right on the DualEntry Accounting AI Benchmark, placing fourth and ahead of every model from Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta. With Zhipu AI's GLM-5.3 Flash tied for second at 88.1%, two of the top four models are now open.

The gap at the top is three points. Google's Gemini 4 Argon leads at 91.1%, and the best open model trails it by 3.0 points. Across the leaderboard, the seven open models average 83.9%, while the 13 closed models average 81.3%.

Key results:

- Kimi K3.1 Pro: 86.1%, fourth overall, up from 84.2% for Moonshot's previous model, Kimi K3
- Best open model: GLM-5.3 Flash at 88.1%, tied for second with Grok 4.7
- Open models hold four of the top seven places
- Bank reconciliation: Kimi K3.1 Pro scored 100%, against 75% for overall leader Gemini 4 Argon
- Cost: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (open) scored 84.2% at $0.003 per task. Claude Fable 5.1 scored 85.1% at $1.18

Closed models still lead on reliability. The top score on hard tasks, 82.1%, is shared by three closed models, and the five models that most often passed a task in all three runs are closed. Gemini 4 Argon leads that measure at 86.1%.

"Finance teams have assumed that choosing an open model meant trading accuracy for cost and control," said Benedict Dohmen of DualEntry. "On accounting work that trade is mostly gone. What's left is consistency, and that is the gap to watch."

The DualEntry Accounting AI Benchmark (DualBench100) tests models on 101 synthetic accounting cases across eight areas: transaction classification, journal entries, financial reporting, bank reconciliation, accounts payable, accounts receivable, month-end close and accounting knowledge. The cases split into 37 easy, 36 medium and 28 hard. Each case has a fixed reference answer and is scored by deterministic rules with an 80% pass mark. Every model runs the full set three times. A task counts as passed when the model passes it in at least two runs. Full results are at dualentry.com/benchmark.

About DualEntry

DualEntry is the agentic, AI-native ERP for mid-market finance teams. It brings the general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, revenue recognition, multi-entity consolidation and reporting into one platform, with AI agents that take on accounting work from data entry through close. Founded in 2024 and based in New York, DualEntry raised a $90 million Series A in 2025 from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures and GV. Learn more at dualentry.com.

Kimi.content:

# Vitalik Buterin Backs AI Model That Deliberately Cut Its Hacking Skills

Updated

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has backed Moonshot AI's decision to strip top-end hacking skills from its new Kimi K3.1 Pro model. In his view, limiting what AI can do beats limiting who may use it.

However, the safeguard comes at a measurable cost. Moonshot says the filtered model solved 81% of tasks on its internal exploit benchmark, while an unfiltered version solved 90.5%.

## Why Vitalik Buterin Prefers AI Limits Over User Checks

Buterin shared his stance, arguing that discriminating against use cases is far less harmful than discriminating against users.

I am okay with Kimi 3.1 deliberately leaving out top-end offensive cyber capabilities from their training data.

Discriminating against use cases is MUCH less bad than discriminating against users. And the world does need all the time it can get to prepare, harden, check old…
— vitalik.eth (@VitalikButerin) October 26, 2026

Moonshot, a Beijing-based AI startup, plans to release the model's open weights by November 4. Anyone can then download it and run it on their own hardware.

Advertisement

Advertisement

For that reason, the company says it removed cyber-related data from its training corpus and reinforcement learning environments. General coding tasks stayed in.

According to Vitalik Buterin, AI-powered attacks will eventually hit at full force. Until then, developers need time to harden systems, check legacy code, and verify new software.

The threat is already visible. Earlier this year, Binance Research found that AI exploits smart contracts roughly twice as well as it detects flaws.

Subscribe to our YouTube channel to watch leaders and journalists provide expert insights

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PqnAlVdpZO8&t=243s

## What Happens if the First Wave of AI Risk Goes Badly

Buterin also warned about the alternative. If this first wave goes badly, he expects locked-down models, Know Your Customer (KYC) checks on everything, and intrusive surveillance.

Advertisement

Advertisement

In that scenario, AI access could depend on credentials and nationality. Some people would become second-, third-, or fourth-class users, he wrote.

Vitalik Buterin has long favored running open AI models on his own hardware, as his local AI laptop tests showed.

Still, he does not expect the filtering to hold forever. When a user asked whether other labs would build such capabilities anyway, he replied that they would.

In fact, by Moonshot's own count, DeepSeek's rival open model V4.1-Flash already scored 85.7% on the same benchmark.

For Vitalik Buterin, AI safety has therefore become a race for time rather than a permanent block. That race favors defenders who adopt his redundant crypto security safeguards before attackers catch up.

# Chinese Open-Weight Model Kimi K3.1 Pro Closes In on U.S. Leaders

Moonshot AI introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro. According to independent benchmarks, the open-weight model competes with leading proprietary U.S. models.

Chinese AI company Moonshot AI has introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro. The system, announced as an open-weight model, is designed to compete in coding, 3D modeling and financial analysis with leading models such as Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra.

Continue after ad

K3.1 Pro builds on Kimi K3, released in July. Its Mixture-of-Experts architecture remains unchanged at 2.8 trillion parameters, with 104 billion active at a time. Its context window still holds up to 1 million tokens, but in Kimi Code this is available only on higher-tier plans. The model processes text, images and videos, and generates text.

Videos by heise

K3.1 Pro is designed to independently execute software projects, develop games, and control Blender and CAD software through its own scripts. It can also create 3D objects from text descriptions, sketches and reference images. With “3D Make”, users can edit the models in a browser and download them for 3D printing. The model can also handle complex financial analyses and evaluate extensive documents. Moonshot says it removed certain training data and tasks to limit offensive cyber capabilities.

## No. 4 in independent AI ranking

Independent tests by Artificial Analysis (AA) show a significant performance jump over its predecessor. K3.1 Pro scores 55 on the Intelligence Index, ranking fourth, compared with 44 for its predecessor. Ahead of it are Claude Opus 5.5 with 58 points and Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Muse Wonder Full with 56 each. With its weights released, K3.1 Pro would currently be the strongest open-weight model in the ranking. According to the technical report, the progress stems mainly from more extensive post-training with reinforcement learning across hundreds of task areas.

The gains are especially pronounced in agentic capabilities. In Terminal-Bench 4.0, the success rate rises from 13% to 67%, the best result in AA’s tests. In AutomationBench-AA, the share of task goals completed in compliance with the rules rises from 58% to 73%. In GDPval-AA, which tests professional tasks, K3.1 Pro scores 1,846 Elo and ranks third, behind Claude Opus 5.5 (1,866) and Muse Wonder Full (1,857). That’s 312 points more than K3.

Continue after ad

In the Humanity’s Last Exam knowledge test, the success rate rises only from 47% to 52%. In the AA-Omniscience test, the hallucination rate falls from 53% to 44%.

### Similar task costs despite lower token prices

Moonshot charges $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through its API, each one-third less than for K3. Cache hits cost 20 cents per million tokens. The Highspeed version, which Moonshot says is two to three times faster, costs $4 and $20, respectively. The price for cache hits remains the same, while writing to the cache costs twice as much.

AA measures about 74 output tokens per second for the standard version, compared with 42 for K3 and 97 for Claude Opus 5.5. The Highspeed version reaches about 129 tokens per second.

Despite lower token prices, task costs are similar: In AA tests, K3.1 Pro generated an average of 55,000 output tokens per Intelligence Index task, 14% more than K3. Under the current model profile, a task costs $2.11, compared with $2.00 for K3 and $5.98 for Claude Opus 5.5 at maximum reasoning effort.

K3.1 Pro is available through Kimi.com and the mobile apps, the Kimi Work desktop agent, the Kimi Code coding tool and Moonshot’s API. The weights are scheduled for release by Nov. 4.

This article was originally published in German. It was translated with technical assistance and editorially reviewed before publication.

开放权重实验室在 2026 年把编码能力与 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 之间的差距越拉越小，Moonshot AI 刚刚又把差距缩小了一步。上周五，Moonshot 发布了 Kimi K3.1 Pro，称其为迄今最强的 3T 级开放权重模型，并在智能体编码上把差距缩小到与 Claude Opus 5.5 仅有 1 分之内。

K3.1 Pro 是 Kimi K3 的重度后训练版本，具备 100 万 token 的上下文窗口。它同时发布了更快的变体 K3.1 Pro Highspeed，并已在 Kimi 应用、Kimi Code 和 Kimi API 上线。完整权重将于 2026 年 11 月 4 日前公布。

要点速览

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 Moonshot 的新旗舰，在 Kimi K3 的基础上进行后训练升级，延续 100 万 token 上下文。

智能体编码是核心亮点：与 Claude Opus 5.5 互有胜负，并在终端工作上优于 GPT-6 Astra。

纯推理与知识类基准仍有差距，与封闭前沿模型相比落后较为明显。

默认使用标准版 K3.1 Pro；仅在延迟比成本更重要时再为 Highspeed 付费。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是什么？

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 Moonshot AI 的旗舰大型语言模型（LLM），也是 K3.1 系列的首款模型。它沿用了 Kimi K3 的基础——一个拥有 2.8T 参数与 100 万 token 上下文窗口的模型，并在此之上加入更多后训练算力。

变化主要在训练而非架构：Moonshot 在其所谓的“数百个下游领域”上联合进行 强化学习（RL），并重构了 RL 框架、沙盒基础设施与 rollout 调度，以确保额外算力带来持续收益。据 Moonshot 称，其测量的所有领域都有提升，尤其是在编码、3D 创作与金融研究方面。

最醒目的主张是：在智能体编码上与最强专有模型实现对标。Moonshot 自家的表格显示，K3.1 Pro 在基于终端的编码任务上与 Claude Opus 5.5 的差距只在 1 分以内，而价格只是 Anthropic 的一小部分。该模型为开放权重，但权重暂未公开。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 关键特性

K3.1 Pro 是一次全面升级，而非单一新技巧。以下四项能力足以让人重新调整工作流。

运行长时、多步骤的编码任务

K3.1 Pro 能够持续推进长时、多步骤的编码任务，能自我诊断失败原因，而不仅仅是重试。Moonshot 展示的案例是基于开源 human-atlas 解剖模型的人体行走模拟器，包含 296 个骨骼与 402 个肌肉组件。

在 167 个任务与 420 次独立评审中，该模型把模拟人从数秒内即倒下，提升为能交替迈步行走 11.2 秒。更有意思的是，当“奖励塑形”不再改善手臂动作时：K3.1 Pro 对模拟器进行了开环探测，发现肩部肌肉力臂计算中有 36 处错误，修复后再训练。

这只是一个内部演示，应将其视为意图用例的说明而非证据。但它展示了 Moonshot 的优化方向：能主动调查并反复迭代的智能体。

更精致地构建游戏、前端与 3D 资产

据 Moonshot 称，K3.1 Pro 生成的前端页面、Three.js 场景与 3D 资产在“版式编排、字体排印、动画与整体打磨”上更胜一筹。它可配合 Unity、Unreal Engine 与 Godot 使用，并能结合网页搜索与 3D 生成来组装完整项目。

在建模方面，K3.1 Pro 可直接为 Blender 与 CAD 软件编写并运行脚本（无需 MCP 连接器），以构建参数化模型，如机械部件、建筑模型与可配置家具。Moonshot 还在 kimi.ai 与 Kimi 应用中上线了 3D Make，您可以在其中预览、编辑并下载可直接 3D 打印的模型。

关于视觉质量的说法也最难用基准表量化验证，因此应把 Moonshot 的演示视为厂商最佳示例，而非平均输出。

以更少的“杜撰”开展金融建模与研究

K3.1 Pro 能把金融工作流从筛选一路推进到成品工作簿，Moonshot 还针对这类工作进行了事实准确性的专项修正。在其内部金融基准上，K3.1 Pro 在 Financial Modeling 上较 Kimi K3 提升 7.2 分，在 Financial Research 上提升 11.6 分，并在 Business Operation（长周期的模拟商业任务）上达到约为 K3 的 4.2 倍。

准确性工作也反映在 Moonshot 的幻觉压力测试中。在 Kimi Hallu Bench Hard 上，K3 的逐条断言幻觉率为 23.4%，而 K3.1 Pro 降至 8.3%。Moonshot 强调该测试旨在诱发错误，因此这些比率并不等同于日常错误率。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 的基准表现如何？

在智能体编码与重工具工作上，Kimi K3.1 Pro 可与 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6 Astra 竞争，但在纯推理方面明显落后。以下数据均来自 Moonshot 的发布公告，K3.1 Pro 的设置为 max。

智能体编码

智能体编码是 K3.1 Pro 最强的领域。在 Terminal-Bench 4.0（以真实、资源受限的终端任务评测编码智能体）上，K3.1 Pro 得分 65.7%。这只比 Claude Opus 5.5 的 66.4% 略低，且明显领先 GPT-6 Astra 的 58.2%。

其余编码结果较标题亮点更为参差。以下成绩均为厂商自报，每行最优分以粗体显示：

在真实终端任务上的编码智能体

20 个多小时工程任务，无网络

113 个长周期任务，按行为评分

从二进制与规格反向重建程序（至少通过 95% 测试的任务）

K3.1 Pro 在长时工程任务上与最强封闭模型打成平手，并在 Moonshot 的 SWE-Marathon 对比中领先。就 DeepSWE 而言，各实验室各用各的设置，3 分的差距更像是平手而非胜出。当需要仅凭观测行为重建程序或推进科研工作流时，它则明显落后。

与前代相比，最清晰的提升体现在 Moonshot 自家的长周期基准上，Kimi K3 当时得分为 55.95%。

工具使用、办公与浏览

在重工具的智能体工作上，K3.1 Pro 领先或与 Opus 5.5 相差仅几个百分点：

HLE-Full（含工具）

2,500 道高难度知识与推理问题，允许用工具

在网页上查找难以定位的信息

跨真实金融 PDF 的数值分析

从筛选到盈利分析的投资工作流

Moonshot 表中一个明显的例外是电脑操作，Opus 5.5 依然领先。在 Frontier Finance 上，Claude Fable 5.1（60.8）总体领先，高于此处展示的四个模型。

推理与知识

在不使用工具时，K3.1 Pro 明显落后于封闭模型：

HLE-Full

2,500 道高难度知识与推理问题

差距在 HLE-Diamond 上最为显著，而 GPQA-Diamond 基本接近“饱和”，2 分的差距意义不大。若您的工作以高难度的闭卷推理为主，这并非值得切换的模型。

网络安全：有意为之

Moonshot 在开放权重发布中做了件不寻常的事：公开了其有意削减的能力幅度。它发现中期训练数据与 RL 环境中的网络安全相关内容会稳步提升漏洞研究能力，因此在开放权重版本中将这类数据从两个阶段都移除。

在 Moonshot 的内部漏洞开发基准 xdev-bench-hard 上，未移除数据的检查点能解决 90.5% 的问题（pass@3）。发布的 K3.1 Pro 能解决 81.0%，仍显著高于 Kimi K3 的 33.3%。在公开网络安全基准上，它低于 Moonshot 对比的所有封闭模型，在 ExploitBench 上得分 74.7，对比 Opus 5.5 的 91.0。

Moonshot 表示其原则是在逐步提升开放权重水平的同时，避免发布在攻防网络安全能力上推动绝对前沿的开放权重。9.5 分的“削减”是否足够，见仁见智，但把数字公之于众已超出许多实验室所做。

应该选择哪个版本？

标准版 K3.1 Pro 对几乎所有人来说都是正确默认。Highspeed 只有在有人在前端等待输出的场景下，才值回其更高的价格。

Default to standard K3.1 Pro and pay for Highspeed only when waiting costs more than tokens

Long agent runs and hard debugging

High-volume batch jobs

Based on Moonshot AI's published variants, reasoning levels, and API pricing, October 2026

Moonshot 对 Highspeed 的卖点只有速度：运行速度快 2–3 倍，输入与输出 token 价格翻倍，且无单独的基准成绩。

两个变体都会在回答前“思考”，且无法关闭。您可以通过三个推理等级来设定强度：max 用于最难的智能体工作，high 作为合理的中档，low 适用于默认思考时间超过任务所需的场景。API 默认使用 max，Moonshot 基准表中的所有成绩都基于该设置，因此除非任务确实需要全力推理，否则请下调至 high 或 low。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 定价与可用性

Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Kimi API 上的价格为每百万输入 token 2.00 美元、每百万输出 token 10.00 美元，低于 Kimi K3。定价在整个 100 万 token 上下文范围内保持统一，不收取长上下文附加费。

以上价格均为每百万 token，未含税。缓存默认自动开启（5 分钟），您也可以在每次调用中申请 1 小时档。

在规划前，以下接入细节值得注意：

API 准入：充值至少 1 美元后解锁 K3.1 Pro，累计充值金额决定您的限流额度。

数据保留：API 客户可选择零数据保留（Zero Data Retention）。

应用：正逐步在 Kimi.ai、iOS、Android 与 HarmonyOS 应用，以及 Kimi Work 桌面应用（3.1.0 版起）上线。

企业版：Kimi Enterprise 管理员需为其组织手动开启 K3.1 Pro；上线时默认关闭。

如果您仍在使用 K2 系列模型，Moonshot 文档称其将于 2026 年 10 月 31 日起不再向新用户提供，并将在 2026 年 12 月底前退役。

如何获取 Kimi K3.1 Pro？

您今天即可通过 Kimi API、OpenRouter 和 Kimi 自家应用使用 Kimi K3.1 Pro，但暂不可下载权重。Moonshot 称完整权重将于 2026 年 11 月 4 日前发布，其公告未提及许可证条款，待权重发布后请查阅模型卡。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 进一步证明开放权重模型能够在智能体编码上匹敌封闭前沿，同时价格低于上一代。它并非通用推理的领跑者，但在长时编码与重工具的智能体工作上，已能紧贴 Claude Opus 5.5，并在多项任务上领先 GPT-6 Astra。

Moonshot 也押注于公开其在网络安全取舍上的做法，为开放发布赢得善意。如果您在用智能体写代码，建议现在通过 API 试用，并在 11 月权重与模型卡发布后再考虑自托管。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 与 Kimi K3 相比如何？

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 Kimi K3 的后训练版本，叠加了大量强化学习。在保留 100 万 token 上下文窗口的同时，编码、金融与事实准确性都有提升：在 Moonshot 的 Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 上得分 61.2%，而 K3 为 55.95%；在 Kimi Hallu Bench Hard 上的逐条断言幻觉率从 23.4% 降至 8.3%。API 价格也更便宜。

我可以在哪里使用 Kimi K3.1 Pro？

Kimi K3.1 Pro 可在 Kimi.ai、Kimi 移动应用、Kimi Work 桌面应用（3.1.0 版及以上）、Kimi Code，以及 Kimi API（kimi-k3.1-pro）中使用。OpenRouter 上的条目为 moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro。Kimi Enterprise 管理员需为其组织手动开启。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 的 API 费用是多少？

Kimi K3.1 Pro 的价格为每百万输入 token 2.00 美元、每百万输出 token 10.00 美元，缓存输入为每百万 0.20 美元。相比之下，Kimi K3 为 3.00 美元与 15.00 美元。定价在整段 100 万 token 上下文内保持统一，API 在充值至少 1 美元后解锁。

我该用 Kimi K3.1 Pro 还是 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed？

默认使用标准版 Kimi K3.1 Pro。Highspeed 仅以速度取胜：运行速度快 2 至 3 倍，没有单独的基准成绩，且输入与输出 token 价格翻倍（每百万分别为 4.00 美元与 20.00 美元），因此只在有人等待响应的交互场景中更划算。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是否开源，权重何时发布？

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是开放权重模型，但权重尚未公开。Moonshot 表示完整权重将于 2026 年 11 月 4 日前发布，其公告未提及许可证条款，请在权重发布后查阅模型卡。在此之前，您只能通过 Kimi 的应用、Kimi API 或 OpenRouter 使用。

# 月之暗面 K3 模型大升級 3 兆級參數規模稱冠全球

本文共656字

經濟日報 記者林宸誼／綜合報導

大陸AI初創企業月之暗面（Moonshot AI）發布新一代旗艦模型Kimi K3.1 Pro，為K3模型首次重大升級，該模型為3兆級參數規模，支持100萬詞元上下文視窗，為目前全球參數規模最大的開源模型。

此外，Kimi K3.1 Pro主打編程（寫程式）、3D創作、金融研究等複雜專業任務，編程能力更勝GPT-6，並計畫於11月4日前開放完整模型權重。

新浪財經報導，月之暗面同步推出高速版Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed，稱智慧水準與標準版相當，但輸出速度可提高約二至三倍。目前兩款模型已透過Kimi官網、App、Kimi Work、Kimi Code及API提供服務。

月之暗面表示，在程式碼、Agent和知識類基準上，K3.1 Pro達到或接近最強閉源模型水平。其中，在編程智能體測試Terminal-Bench 4.0中，Kimi K3.1 Pro獲得65.7%的評估得分，高於OpenAI的GPT-6 Astra的58.2%，與Anthropic的Claude Opus 5.5的66.4%僅有微弱差距。

彭博形容，月之暗面這次發布新版本，將繼續與DeepSeek和智譜等對手競逐，同時該模型顯著提升金融研究和編程能力，也是美國競爭對手重點發力的方向。

另一方面， 月之暗面近期完成了最後一輪私募融資，估值約500億美元，預計明年第1季在香港上市；策略與規模更大的DeepSeek類似，DeepSeek剛完成一輪150億美元融資，為大陸AI實驗室中至今規模最大的一輪融資，而且該公司正準備上市。

Kimi.content:
# Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro Takes Aim at US AI Leaders

Published on: Oct 26, 2026

Author: Maya Trent

Moonshot AI has pushed its latest Kimi model into the global AI arms race with a release that is drawing comparisons to top-tier U.S. systems, even as the company says it wants to keep cyber capability in check. The Chinese startup released Kimi K3.1 Pro on October 24, describing it as a 3-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model with a 1-million-token context window. On benchmark tables cited by multiple outlets, it lands in the same conversation as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, while Moonshot says the full model weights are due by November 4.

### A Bigger Model, A Sharper Message

Moonshot’s framing is simple: more capability, but with guardrails. In a company statement carried by Indian Express, the firm said, “We aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability.” It also said, “We’re introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window.” That combination is the point of the launch: aggressive scale, open-weight distribution and a public promise not to push cyber powers as far as possible.

The new model is a post-training upgrade of Kimi K3, which was released on July 17, 2026. The earlier model was described as 2.8T parameters. Moonshot’s latest release is being presented as the next step in that line, and the company plans to publish the full weights by November 4, 2026. For AI watchers, that date matters because open-weight releases can quickly spread through developer circles, cloud providers and startup competitors looking for a lower-cost way to catch up.

### Benchmarks Put It Near the Top

The early benchmark story is where the drama starts. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, K3.1 Pro scored 65.7%, according to ANI and ITHome. That puts it above GPT-6 Astra at 58.2% and just below Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4%. In other words, Moonshot is not claiming a distant second-tier slot. It is trying to show that a Chinese open-weight system can run alongside the best-known U.S. frontier models on a difficult benchmark tied to terminal-based tasks.

A second scorecard adds to that message. On Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2, K3.1 Pro scored 55, above Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 4 Argon, which were all at 53, according to Gigazine. Benchmarks are not the same as broad real-world superiority, and they do not settle the model race on their own. But in a market where model quality is often judged by public ranking tables, even small gaps can drive attention, developer testing and enterprise curiosity.

### Cyber Capability, Dialed Back

Moonshot’s launch comes with a notable caveat. The company said it removed cyber-offensive training data, and Indian Express reported that this cut Moonshot’s internal cyber benchmark from 90.5% to 81.0%. That is a rare move in the current AI race, where many companies are trying to maximize capability across coding, reasoning and agentic tasks. Moonshot is signaling that it wants strong performance without being accused of releasing a model that meaningfully widens offensive security risk.

That trade-off may be as important as the benchmark scores. The company is effectively telling regulators, customers and rivals that it sees cyber limits as part of product design, not just a policy afterthought. For enterprise buyers, that could be a selling point. For researchers and model developers, it is also a reminder that the sharpest systems are increasingly being shaped by safety choices as much as raw scale. The question is whether that restraint dulls the model enough to matter in practice.

### Pricing Signals a Commercial Push

Moonshot is also using price to make its case. API pricing is listed at $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens, according to Gigazine and ITHome. That is the kind of pricing detail that can matter almost as much as benchmark talk, because it shapes whether developers experiment with the model in production settings rather than just on paper. Open-weight systems often compete not only on performance but on the cost of deployment, customization and retrieval.

The 1-million-token context window is another commercial hook. Very large context windows are especially attractive for long documents, codebases, legal text, research workflows and agent systems that need to hold more information in memory at once. Moonshot is not just pitching a smarter model; it is pitching one that can handle bigger jobs with less prompt fragmentation. That can help it stand out in a crowded field where many models still struggle to combine long context, speed and reliability without steep costs.

### What the Launch Says About China’s AI Race

K3.1 Pro also highlights how Chinese AI companies are narrowing the gap in public benchmark politics, not just in private engineering. Moonshot is positioning itself against the most visible U.S. systems with a release that is open-weight, low-priced and aggressively benchmarked. That is a strategic mix: it invites independent testing, encourages developer adoption and puts pressure on rivals that rely on closed distribution. For investors watching the AI stack, that matters because model quality is only one part of the business equation.

The unresolved parameter-count dispute around the model may be less important than the broader signal. Some coverage describes K3.1 Pro as 3-trillion-parameter-class, while other references tied to Moonshot’s own material and Gigazine describe K3 with 2.8T total and 104B active parameters. Either way, the launch sits in the same scale bracket as the biggest models being discussed globally. Moonshot is not trying to win by being modest. It is trying to force its way into the same tier as the market leaders.

### No Clean Market Read-Through Yet

For now, there is no verified market reaction specific to the October 24 K3.1 Pro launch. That matters because model announcements often get traded through proxies, especially when investors think a new release could shift cloud demand, enterprise spending or sentiment around AI infrastructure names. But without verified price action tied to this event, the story remains a technology and positioning event rather than an immediate market catalyst.

The earlier July 17 launch of Kimi K3 did trigger sharp moves in a separate episode, with rival Z.AI shares falling 28% and MiniMax down 16%, while the Nasdaq 100 was down 1.5%, according to Bloomberg via The Star. That was a different event, and it should not be confused with the current release. What Moonshot has done now is more subtle but potentially more durable: it has put a more capable model, at public prices, into the same benchmark fight as the U.S. frontier, and it has done so with a safety message attached.

The real test starts on November 4, when Moonshot plans to publish the full model weights. Until then, Kimi K3.1 Pro is a claim backed by benchmark tables, pricing and a clear message about cyber limits. If the model holds up outside company-controlled demonstrations, it could become one of the more closely watched open-weight releases of the year.

# Elon Musk's Grok releases the first 7 minutes of its AI-generated Odyssey film

## Elon Musk promised a historically accurate AI movie, but Grok's first 7-minute 'Odyssey' clip is being slammed by viewers as lifeless and boring.

Advertisement

Elon Musk’s Grok released a seven-minute AI movie based on The Odyssey epic

Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence platform, Grok, has officially stepped into the movie business. Three months after Musk promised to make a full-length, "historically accurate" film by the end of 2026, the Grok Imagine account on X has released a 7-minute video. The company is calling this "Episode 1 of our Odyssey series," which is based on the ancient Greek epic.

The short is based on the ancient Greek epic and was published on X as the first installment of a planned series, not as the full feature film Musk originally promised.

advertisement

### How was it made?

The 7-minute short film was created in partnership with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker. The impressive part is the technology behind it. Grok handled the entire film-making process.

The video was generated using Grok Imagine, xAI’s AI image-and-video tool. However, xAI has not publicly provided a detailed production breakdown confirming exactly how the script, visuals, voices, and camera work were produced.

### What is in the video?

The video shows the Greek hero Odysseus preparing to leave for the Trojan War. It features scenes of his wife, Penelope, encouraging him to go, Greek ships sailing away, and his son, Telemachus, training to fight.

Some parts of the video look very real. The shots of the ships at sea, for example, are so good that viewers might mistake them for live-action footage. However, despite Musk's focus on "historical accuracy," the characters do not speak in ancient Greek. Instead, the narrator and the characters use generic British accents that sound like they belong in a video game.

### The Christopher Nolan drama

This AI movie release comes with a lot of background drama. In July, famous Hollywood director Christopher Nolan released his own live-action version of "The Odyssey." Nolan’s movie was a massive box-office hit, selling out IMAX theatres for months and becoming a top contender for the Academy Awards. It was a huge real-world project, shot across six countries with thousands of crew members.

Elon Musk heavily criticized Nolan’s movie for casting nonwhite and transgender actors. As a response, Grok's AI version features characters with a "Musk-approved" skin colour. Nolan, meanwhile, has openly called himself a "techno-skeptic" and criticized how much the public has rejected AI.

### Why are people rejecting the AI movie?

Even though the AI video looks visually decent, the overall reaction has been very negative. Reviewers and social media users have pointed out that the movie completely lacks a human touch, artistry, and emotion.

Critics have called the dialogue stiff and the background narration far too long. While Nolan's three-hour movie kept audiences hooked, viewers found themselves getting bored just halfway through Grok's 7-minute clip. Many users on X criticized the pacing and called the video "slop," comparing it to a boring video game cutscene that you just want to skip.

It is still a mystery when the full-length movie that Musk promised will actually come out. For now, it seems the AI still has a long way to go before it can replace real human actors and directors.

- Ends

### Christina Applegate Says She Was Misdiagnosed With Multiple Sclerosis: ‘It’s Very Confusing’

Oct 20, 2026

Five years after Christina Applegate‘s doctors told her that she had multiple sclerosis, they’re now telling her she never had the autoimmune disorder. The actress revealed the news on MeSsy, her MS-themed podcast she hosts with Jamie Lynn Sigler, who has MS, since March 2024. She said she’s in a “state of shock” over the news, which she calls a “mindfuck.” What’s most frustrating for Applegate, though, is that she still has symptoms that no longer have an explanation and that she feels she accidentally misrepresented herself to those with the disorder, according to People.

On back-to-back episodes of the podcast, Applegate explained that she took a leave of absence from the podcast in March while she processed her doctor’s news. “She came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’” Applegate said. “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”

Dr. Marwa Kaisey, who works in Cedars-Sinai Medical Center’s neurology department, spoke on the podcast saying misdiagnoses are “fairly common” since there is no single binary MS test saying whether a patient definitely has or doesn’t have the disorder. “Almost one in five of these people who’d been told they had MS, some for decades, didn’t actually have it,” the physician said. “And a majority of them were on medication to treat their MS.”

Multiple sclerosis damages the protective cover around one’s nerves, according to the Cleveland Clinic. It can cause “muscle weakness, vision changes, numbness and memory issues.”

“It’s weird because I feel like I let everybody down,” Applegate said on one of the episodes. “It’s this weird feeling because I became this — you [Sigler] and I, the poster children for MS. And everything I was doing. I had a reason. I had a fucking reason as to why my day sucked every day. And now I don’t have a reason and it’s very unnerving and it’s very confusing for me.” She described her present state as “the same game with a different name.”

Applegate said she feels like her symptoms have gotten worse since she learned the news. “You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I’m better,” Applegate said. She added that she expects her doctors to investigate how and why she was misdiagnosed.

“I still have to use wheelchairs when I go to the doctor’s office,” she said. “I can’t walk from the car to the room. I’m still in this. Nothing magical happened when she said, ‘You don’t have MS.’ Nothing magical happened.”

Applegate has spoken at length about MS, saying in 2024 that she believed she had been suffering from the disorder at least six or seven years prior to the 2021 diagnosis. “I noticed, especially the first season [of the Netflix series Dead to Me], we’d be shooting, and my leg would buckle,” she said at the time on Good Morning America. “I really just put it off as being tired, or I’m dehydrated, or it’s the weather. Then, nothing would happen for months, and I didn’t pay attention. But when it hit this hard, I had to pay attention.”

Applegate announced her retirement from acting on camera in 2023, saying then that she would focus on voice work. She teared up onstage in 2024 when she received a standing ovation at the Emmys while presenting an award. “You’re totally shaming me by standing up!” Applegate said, clinging to Anthony Anderson’s arm.

“I’ve gone through a great depression because of [the misdiagnosis],” Applegate said on MeSsy. “But I lost everything. I lost my job. I lost — I’m sorry. What do you say to someone who’s been living with this for six years — God, I’m so sorry — because it stopped my life.”

Text Size:

New Delhi: Elon Musk’s AI platform Grok has released a seven-minute episode of an AI-generated adaptation of Homer’s The Odyssey, months after the billionaire promised to create a full length film based on the ancient Greek epic by the end of 2026. Released on X on 23 October, the clip marks the first instalment of a project Musk announced in July after criticising filmmaker Christopher Nolan’s adaptation of the epic.

Watch Episode 1  of our Odyssey series made with Grok Imagine.

Creative collaboration with @WonderStudiosX and director Dev Walker @glumlot_ pic.twitter.com/xpgpkqSCpq

— Grok Imagine (@imagine) October 23, 2026

The episode was shared by the Grok Imagine account on X and credited to Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker. In July, ahead of Nolan’s magnum opus, Musk announced the project with a three-minute-long AI-generated video inspired by the epic.

“Before this year ends, Grok Imagine will make a full-length movie of The Odyssey that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer,” he wrote on X.

Before this year ends, Grok Imagine will make a full-length movie of The Odyssey that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer https://t.co/bVHzUmY9WN

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) July 22, 2026

However, fans online were not impressed. “It supposed to be historically correct. Why are they talking in English?” a user pointed out. Another user took a dig at the trailer and wrote, “It’s gonna be historically accurate Belt buckles, Medieval tunics and late Roman cloaks, Romanesque arches, zero Greek or Mycenaean mural paintings, everyone is dirty all the time… this is the worst kind of slop.”

Many fans also equated the episode to an AI slop. An X user wrote, “Now that’s garbage Al slop, totally unrealistic, a cartoon would be more realistic than this.” At the same time, another user wrote, “Hard pass. AI will never replace the talent of actors, writers, directors and editors,” second user commented

However, the seven-minute-long episode is a limited first release rather than the full length film Musk had promised. Further details about the production schedule and the release of the complete adaptation have not been announced.

Musk’s criticism of Nolan’s The Odyssey, starring Matt Damon, centred on the casting of Lupita Nyong’o as Helen of Troy. The choice sparked a debate among fans, some of whom argued that Homer described Helen as “white-armed” in the original text.

Critics accused Hollywood of continuing its long standing practice of “race-swapping” by casting a Black actress in the role. Musk joined the criticism after the film’s first trailer was released, calling Nolan an “anti-white racist” and accusing the filmmaker of compromising his integrity. Like other critics, Musk alleged that the casting decision was motivated by a desire to secure an Academy Award.

“Chris Nolan desecrated the Odyssey so that he would be eligible for an Academy Award,” he said.

Chris Nolan desecrated the Odyssey so that he would be eligible for an Academy Award …

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) May 15, 2026

Elon here referred to the eligibility criteria that every film should meet to get nominated for an Academy Award. A film must satisfy two out of four standards set by the Academy, which include conditions such as actor ethnicity, having women and LGBTQIA+ members in the ensemble cast, the main storyline being centred on an underrepresented group, and many more.

xAI 旗下 AI 影片工具 Grok Imagine 在 X 平台發布 AI 生成版《奧德賽》(The Odyssey)首集,片長約 7 分鐘,並與 Wonder Studios 及導演 Dev Walker 合作製作。Elon Musk 7 月曾承諾年底前推出完整長片,現階段只公開系列第一集。

## 首集內容與製作團隊

Grok Imagine 帳號在 10 月 23 日(星期五)發布影片,稱之為「Odyssey 系列第 1 集」,並註明是與 Wonder Studios 及導演 Dev Walker 的創意合作。Variety 指出,Wonder Studios 與 Dev Walker 都專注 AI 電影製作。TechCrunch 形容片中有人物在海上航行,並由英式口音旁白交代背景故事,片中角色沒有說古希臘語。

## Musk 7 月曾承諾製作長片

Musk 7 月宣布,Grok Imagine 會在年底前製作一部「史實準確、忠於荷馬藝術」的《奧德賽》長片,當時附上一段由 X 用戶製作的 3 分鐘 AI 短片。Variety 形容今次發布是 Musk「部分兌現」承諾,而帳號並無附上其他說明。

## 與 Nolan 版《奧德賽》的背景

Musk 在 Christopher Nolan 版《奧德賽》上映前,多次批評影片選角,包括 Elliot Page 飾演 Sinon、Lupita Nyong’o 飾演 Helen of Troy。TechCrunch 指 Nolan 版 7 月上映後票房大收,Imax 場次連月爆滿,並有望成為下屆奧斯卡熱門。

## 外界評價

TechCrunch 認為部分鏡頭接近真實,畫面比 Musk 近期發布其他影片更出色,但整體缺乏藝術感、靈感和人情味,節奏停滯,角色對白生硬。Variety 則引述導演 Scott Derrickson 7 月時在 X 的批評,他指 Musk 不懂電影,對藝術的意見毫無價值。以上均為相關媒體及人士的評論,並非官方說法。
