# Elon Musk’s AI-Generated ‘Odyssey’ Is Here to Save Western Civilization

“Homer didn’t have Grok. We do.”

Reading time 3 minutes

Imagine somehow being able to tell Homer, as he set pen to paper to start work on The Odyssey, that thousands of years into the future, his epic tale of Odysseus’ long, strange journey home from the Trojan War would become the latest battleground in another war—one that would manage to be even more stupid and pointless than the one from which his hero was politely excusing himself.

Yes, people, Elon Musk’s Grok-powered Odyssey has arrived, and it’s ready to strap on its bronze armor and charge forth in a heroic bid to save Western civilization from the dastardly forces of the Woke, the Feminists and the Historically Inaccurate Presence of People Who Look Suspiciously Black. Marvel at the bravery of this artistic vision! Thrill to its battlecry of “ουέλ άκτουλλι!” Cower as an entire website army full of weird nerds unleashes its righteous rage on Hollywood!

Watch Episode 1  of our Odyssey series made with Grok Imagine.

Let us know in the comments if you'd like a full breakdown of how it was done!

Creative collaboration with @WonderStudiosX and director Dev Walker @glumlot_ pic.twitter.com/xpgpkqSCpq

— Grok Imagine (@imagine) October 23, 2026

…for seven minutes, anyway. While Musk promised an entire feature-length rival to Christopher Nolan’s version of The Odyssey, what arrived over the weekend was no such thing—instead, it was billed as “Episode 1 of our Odyssey series.” Turns out that making movies maybe isn’t quite as easy as typing “Make The Odyssey but without anything that would upset people who are still mad about Gamergate,” even with the backing of the world’s richest man and his favorite toy.

In fairness, the footage shows how far AI-powered video has come since the hilarity of its early days—which were only a couple of years ago, god help us—but it also shows that there’s a world of difference between making something that looks kinda cinematic and making something that is worth watching. Sure, the landscapes look realistic, even if the wide shots are a bit ropey, while the baby is only vaguely terrifying and everyone has the correct number of fingers. Great!

But this is meant to be more than a tech demo; it’s meant to be proof that Grok is liberating filmmaking from the grasp of the libs. So is it a good film? Well, no. It’s not a good film in the slightest. If anything, it reads more like a trailer or the overlong intro to a video game, the kind you skip halfway through the first viewing and then install a mod so you don’t have to smash the space bar every time.

There’s no coherent narrative; instead, it’s just a selection of portentous shots, all of which allude to a story rather than try to actually tell it. Odysseus hits a table because Odysseus is mad! The Greeks yell “vengeance!” because they want vengeance! Penelope calls Odysseus “my love” and tells him that he must go to war, even though it’s dumb and he doesn’t want to, because she’s a dutiful tradwife! The obligatory overconfident joker dude pukes off the side of a boat because he’s actually a big pansy! A shot of lil Telemachus learning to fight back home is juxtaposed against the Madness Of War™ IRL, because the intended audience is dumb as a rock! And so on and so forth.

The only surprise is that the whole masturbatory enterprise doesn’t end with a Cybertruck thundering across the battlefield so that Elon can hang himself out the window and give a Nazi salute. Maybe the Cybertruck got stuck in the mud. Or maybe that’s scheduled for Part 2—assuming that there is in fact a Part 2, because god knows it’s hard to imagine that anyone would volunteer to sit through more of this. But then again, there are plenty of people who choose of their own free will to pay real actual money for blue checks on Twitter, so who knows.

Anyway, as Wonder Studios, the people behind this silliness, boast in their tweet announcing its release: “Homer didn’t have Grok. We do.” Yeah. It shows.

# Canva Wants to Destroy Traditional AI Image Generators With This One Trick

An Australian design software giant called Canva has released its first in-house image generation model named Craft. The company built the model from scratch through its internal research lab to improve creative control and reduce operating costs.

Unlike standard image generators that learn primarily from raw photographs, Craft was trained on millions of human-made templates. Specifically, the training data includes professional presentations, infographics, posters, and menus from Canva’s vast content library. As a result, the model learns fundamental design principles like visual hierarchy, margins, and type size.

“We started by creating flat images with diffusion models. Omni models have taken that a step further, where you’re able to edit those flat images with a lot of sophistication through prompting. But the tools have made you prompt your way to the final result, which, for a visual medium, is challenging,” Canva’s global head of product, Robert Kawalsky said to the media. “What we’ve found is that people . . . want the ability to start with a prompt and get far, but also be able to iterate directly themselves.”

The software utilizes a unique two-stage architecture. First, an internal planning model interprets the user prompt to map out spatial relationships, element placement, and required text. Then, a rendering engine turns that structural blueprint into a finished picture. Because of this workflow, the model produces highly legible typography and clean layouts compared to traditional single-pass tools.

The system supports outputs up to 2K resolution across more than thirty different aspect ratios. In addition, generated assets integrate smoothly with Canva’s editing suite, allowing creators to modify individual text or graphic layers easily.

Platform executives noted that managing external AI tools became increasingly expensive as user demand surged. Therefore, building proprietary infrastructure helps the company lower API expenses and secure long-term profit margins. Furthermore, researchers from Leonardo.ai, a media-generation platform that Canva acquired earlier, contributed directly to the development process.

Initial benchmarking results place Craft strongly among industry competitors on evaluation leaderboards. Meanwhile, development teams are already working on lighter variants named Craft-fast and Craft-ultrafast to speed up generation times further.

Ultimately, this launch gives millions of global users a specialized tool designed specifically for professional marketing and everyday design workflows.

# 韩国游戏巨头 KRAFTON 放出 Raon-1 mini，叫板 Meta 同档模型

韩国游戏企业 KRAFTON（魁匠团）旗下的人工智能分支 KRAFTON AI 本周公布了 Raon-1 mini 的预览版本。这是一款从零训练起来的模型，正式版和更大的后续型号已在路上。在巨头林立的基础模型赛道，一家游戏公司拿出自有模型，本身就透着跨界野心。

30B-A4B 的"小而全"

Raon-1 mini 采用混合专家（MoE）架构，并引入线性注意力、支持推测解码，整体体量标注为 30B-A4B——即总参数约 300 亿，单次激活约 40 亿。它在主攻韩语的同时兼顾英语，并以 Apache 2.0 许可开源，官网还挂出了限时免费的 API 试用。

KRAFTON AI 给出的成绩单很直白：预览版在编程与智能体任务上，与 Meta 的 Muse Glimmer 30B 处在同一水平，但跑得更快、吃内存更省，还能进行自然的对话。换句话说，它想在同一体量段里，用效率和性价比撕开一道口子。

游戏公司为何卷模型

一家靠《绝地求生》起家的游戏厂亲自下场训模型，背后不难理解。游戏研发本身对剧情生成、NPC 对话、美术与代码辅助需求旺盛，自研底座既能压成本也能把可控性握在手里；而把模型开源、放出试用，又是低成本攒口碑、拉开发者和生态的好法子。

当 Meta、谷歌等巨头把基础模型越做越大，KRAFTON 选择从 30B 这一"够用且好部署"的档位切入，瞄准的或许是既想要本地化韩语能力、又不愿被巨头绑定的一批用户。Raon-1 mini 能否兑现承诺，正式版与更大模型的表现将是关键注脚，也为"游戏厂也能做好底座"这一命题写下第一笔。

# From "Competing on Model Development" to "Seizing Entry Points": Domestic large AI models march into the consumer hardware sector

司库商业2026-10-26 08:53

Domestic large models are beginning to shift.

In 2026, domestic large models in China have started to "deviate from their supposed core business": on October 13th, StepVerse and Alibaba Qwen released AI-focused smartphones, glasses and earphone products on the very same day.

It is by no means a coincidence that the two large model vendors launched consumer electronics products on the same day, which marks the vane of domestic AI large model development in China — the competition between vendors will no longer be limited to the performance parameters of the latest version of AI large models, nor the price and cost of products, but will extend to consumer hardware terminals.

Why did large model vendors rush to cross-border to develop consumer-grade hardware products in 2026?

The reason is quite simple, the iteration speed of AI large models is getting faster and faster, which leads to a common problem faced by all major vendors: they cannot retain users and realize monetization. Therefore, seizing hardware entrances such as smartphones and smart glasses has become a mandatory task.

However, when a large number of software application companies swarm into developing consumer-grade AI hardware, can they really form a closed loop to retain the lost users?

## 【1】Anxiety under fierce competition

In China's technology industry, AI large model is the most popular sector, bar none. Data released by the Cyberspace Administration of China shows that:

As of July 2026, the total number of large models released in China has reached 1509, ranking first in the world; in the first half of 2026 alone, the total financing amount in the AI sector reached 4544.9 billion yuan, almost twice that of last year.

From the data perspective, the AI large model industry seems to be in a golden age of prosperity and booming development.

But just like the novel *Fortress Besieged*, outsiders only see the bright side, while insiders know all too well the hardships behind these figures — the industry is extremely involuted, so much so that even a slight lag will lead to the loss of users.

According to statistics from *New Wisdom*, from the beginning of this year to September 22, ten major vendors including Doubao, Alibaba Qwen and DEEPSEEK have released at least 28 flagship models in total, with a new domestic large model launched every 9.5 days on average.

(Source: New Wisdom)

In terms of price, in the first half of 2026, there were six rounds of price cuts in the industry, with the cumulative decline exceeding the sum of all price cuts from the beginning of 2024 to the end of 2025.

It is not hard to see that the involution in performance and price is driving the continuous development of the entire large model industry, which is a good thing at the macro level, forcing all major domestic large model vendors to improve their competitiveness.

But it is not necessarily a good thing for large model vendors — this competition featuring extremely fast iteration speed makes it impossible for vendors to retain users, who will only flow to large model products with better intelligent experience and lower cost.

Data from QuestMobile shows that from January to February this year, the first-day retention rate of mainstream domestic AI applications was 65%, but when the time horizon is extended, the 15-day retention rate is only 18%, and the 30-day retention rate is only 12.8%.

It should be noted that to make profits, a product must first have a certain number of core user base. Only when the core user base reaches a certain scale can the enterprise have room for growth and realize commercial monetization through value-added services.

For example, providing services such as product recommendations or localized food, entertainment and leisure recommendations based on user environment, behavior and preference data; providing office assistants based on users' language habits and work styles.

All the above visions are based on the premise that users are deeply dependent on a certain large model. But obviously, in this booming wave of diverse products, what domestic large model vendors lack most is user loyalty and stickiness.

## 【2】Betting on consumer-grade hardware entrances

To fix the loopholes, we need to make up for the shortcomings. How to solve the problem of user loss? Domestic large model vendors have set their sights on consumer hardware.

The reason is very simple. First, the iteration speed of domestic large models is too fast, so users will naturally flow to the large model applications with the highest test rankings and best performance. Second, for software products, the cost for users to switch is almost zero.

Consumer-grade AI hardware can just solve these two problems. Whether it is AI glasses or smartphones equipped with intelligent agents, users will hold and use them for a long time. This means that once users start using their own AI hardware products, it will be very difficult for them to churn due to factors such as high switching costs.

"AI that stays at the App level will always be a 'tenant'. Only by developing hardware on its own can AI become a 'native resident'", the statement from Yin Qi, CEO of StepVerse, is the most straightforward. Only by securing consumer-grade AI hardware can large model vendors achieve long-term user retention.

In fact, Yin Qi's hardware philosophy has long become the industry consensus:

In December 2025, ByteDance teamed up with ZTE Nubia to launch the nubia M153 equipped with Doubao mobile assistant. In September this year, the Doubao smartphone hit the market, with more than 360,000 reservations on JD.com. ByteDance also jointly released the "Lingxi Xinghuo Smart Box" series with China Mobile, covering hardware forms such as AI office laptops, AI voice recorders and AIPC;

In July, StepVerse released "STEPX", a native large model AI terminal brand, and its first self-developed smartphone STEPX Neo, with a built-in personal intelligent agent Amoo. On October 13, the "Pioneer Version" of STEPX Neo was officially released, with a full-stack pricing of 3999 yuan. Amoo can independently plan and schedule corresponding services across applications, and complete a variety of tasks such as ticket booking, office work, video editing and local life services in one stop;

(Source: StepVerse official website)

In October, Alibaba released Qwen AI Glasses N1/N1 Pro with built-in daily "Personal Agent" and its first Qwen AI ear-clip headphone. According to a report by *LatePost*, following the AI glasses, the Wuying team under Alibaba Cloud is testing an AI tablet device named QwenBook, positioned as a native intelligent agent computer, whose full version is expected to be released at the end of 2026 or early 2027.

From ByteDance's Doubao to StepVerse and Alibaba Qwen, all of them launched consumer-grade AI hardware in the first half of 2026. It is obvious that self-developed consumer-grade hardware has become the major trend for domestic AI large model vendors.

## 【3】New challenges facing the ideal blueprint

In fact, many AI large model vendors attribute problems such as user churn and difficulty in commercial monetization to the lack of consumer-grade AI hardware, trying to retain users through terminal hardware products and build an ecosystem centered on their own large models.

The vision is very beautiful, but is it really easy to realize this grand blueprint where consumer hardware feeds back software applications? I don't think so.

First of all, there are constraints from limited resources. Consumer products such as AI smartphones and AI glasses involve many links including supply chain, R&D, spare parts stockpiling and so on, which will inevitably consume the manpower and capital of large model enterprises.

It should be noted that the current large model industry features an iteration speed of "overnight updates". If large model vendors disperse their energy to cross-border into hardware development, for example, in 2025, Zhipu AI's revenue was only 724 million yuan, while its net loss reached 4.718 billion yuan, with the loss 6.5 times its revenue; MiniMax's total revenue was 79.038 million US dollars, while its total loss within the year reached 1.872 billion US dollars...

Even for large manufacturers like ByteDance that have sufficient capital, the Doubao smartphone is not fully developed on its own, but cooperated with ZTE Nubia. For independent large model companies like StepVerse, facing continuous losses on one hand, and high investment and high failure rate of consumer hardware on the other, the pressure of independently developing consumer-grade AI hardware can be imagined.

Secondly, in addition to large model vendors developing AI hardware, hardware manufacturers are also launching their own AI large models and implanting them into their own products.

For example, Xiaomi's MiMo series. In this year's September Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro scored 46 points, surpassing Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, ranking first among global open-source models and first among domestic models.

(Source: Xiaomi MiMo official website)

More importantly, the MiMo large model has been implanted into all of Xiaomi's hardware products. For example, Xiaomi 18 Fold and Xiaomi 18 Pro are equipped with the super Xiaoai 2.0 powered by MiMo on-device large model; its first AI native smartphone code-named "Lobster" has entered the closed beta testing stage...

Facing players like Xiaomi that have strong hardware capabilities and excellent software performance, how domestic large model vendors can attract users and gain competitive advantages through the strengths of AI software is the key focus of the industry in the future.

This terminal competition in 2026, on the surface, is a competition over the forms of smartphones,

# Mistral Large 4 Weights: The Final Week

The Introducing Mistral Large 4 page has said the same thing since October 6: "Weights drop end of this month," and, more fully, "We will release the weights by the end of the month, along with more details on the architecture, additional benchmarks, and our post-training methodology." That is the whole of the vendor's written commitment – no day, no hour. On Day 26 of 31 in Mistral's own month-end window, three clocks are running anyway. The first is October 27: the date Reuters reported on October 6, carried here after its own URL returned a 401 at fetch and the date was confirmed through search extraction and secondary coverage explicitly citing the wire – reported, and never put on the record by Mistral. The second is that undated sentence. The third is the Hugging Face card, fetch-verified October 26: an "Upcoming release" badge, a countdown reading 05 days, 00 hours, 13 minutes to October 31 at 15:00Z, and a Current ETA stamp whose tooltip says "The release date may still change." This desk mapped the same pegs two days ago; the compression has only tightened since.

The wait list is the one measurable moving part: 813 people waiting on October 14, 939 on October 24, 951 by the October 26 fetch. Interest is compounding into the final week while the artifacts stay put. The repository still lists a single planned artifact, and both the open weights and the LICENSE file are absent from the first-party surface – absence certified at the surface we checked, not inferred. Mistral is spending the window red-teaming the model "with cybersecurity leaders, vetted partners, and state authorities, who will access the same model with reduced moderation and expanded cyber capabilities." That work proceeds on a schedule the public calendar cannot see, which is precisely the problem a countdown is supposed to solve and does not.

Planning around that invisibility already has a price tag this month. StepFun's September 20 promise targeted an October 15 release; when the date arrived, the expected repository returned a 404 and the license was still unpublished – the vendor-promise class's first exhibit. Teams that had pre-allocated clusters and engineering time ate the slip as idle hardware. Mistral's signal is stronger than StepFun's was: a dated card plus a month-end sentence, not a bare day. But a reliability class is a reliability class. Reported and projected are not committed, and the card says so in its own tooltip.

Advertisement

Advertisement

The calendar is the half of this release that expires. The decision that outlives it is the license. Mistral Large 3 shipped under permissive Apache 2.0; this desk's own license countdown reported the industry expectation that Mistral Large 4 arrives under a custom framework instead – which would place the new weights inside the convention already documented across the four-lab revenue gate. Mistral's existing Modified MIT terms, in place since August, already push companies with monthly revenue above $20 million into a commercial license or through Mistral Studio. What is unknown is narrower and more consequential than the date: whether the new model's LICENSE repeats that gate, moves it, or does something the precedent does not prepare builders for. The file does not exist yet, so no claim about its terms is available to make. The absence is the fact.

That gives deployers a cleaner rule than the countdown offers. Gate migration scheduling, procurement review, and compliance work on the fetch of a LICENSE file, not on a timer the vendor has explicitly reserved the right to move. Weights landing without terms would repeat the StepFun shape: a repository you cannot deploy from. Terms landing without the weights would matter more than the weights themselves. When the artifact finally appears, the first question is not whether the countdown reached zero. It is what the document says your revenue obligates you to do.

# Swedish startup Strawberry launches AI agent platform and preps Series A funding round

S
Scott Thompson | 26 Oct 2026 
Strawberry, a startup with $6 million in funding from EQT and General Catalyst, has launched 1.0 of its AI agent platform built for non-technical teams, such as sales, recruiting, customer support and marketing.

It is free to try and lets users and teams create their own virtual colleagues, called AI companions. According to Strawberry, unlike chatbots such as Claude and ChatGPT, which take a prompt and complete a task, companions work like real colleagues, alongside people and not instead of them. It operates as a browser, where a team's context, workflows and logins already live. A companion remembers how your team works and gets better the more you work together, because it is connected to all of that context.

"The technology is already here: agents can now work for weeks in a row. Yet, we see so many companies struggle with adoption. We built a product so delightful that teams adopt it naturally, with companions you bring into your team like colleagues," says Charles Maddock, CEO and Co-founder at Strawberry.

"Today the person who is great with Claude keeps all of it on their own laptop. In Strawberry you train a companion once, and everyone on the team gets it, with everything it has learned. The browser is fast becoming the front line for AI, and the Strawberry team is at the centre of that shift," saysYuri Sagalov, Partner, General Catalyst.

The Stockholm, Sweden-based company plans to follow this launch with a Series A funding round.

# Will Nuix (ASX:NXL) Agentic AI Launch Lift Neo Growth?

5 min read | October 26, 2026 12:15 PM AEDT | By Sam

### Highlights
- Nuix released an AI agent inside its Neo platform that answers plain-language questions and records every step so investigators can check the reasoning.
- The latest annual result showed revenue growth, a return to statutory earnings and rapid expansion in contract value tied to Neo.
- The shares have fallen over the past year, and an appeal in a regulatory case against the company is still pending.

Nuix (ASX:NXL) Technology NUIX Ltd (ASX:NXL) 1.89 AUD +0.040 2.168% Last Updated at: 2026-10-26T00:52:00Z has launched an AI agent inside its Neo investigations platform that shows its working, a pitch aimed at lawyers, auditors and regulators who need to explain to a court or board how an answer was reached. Nuix is a constituent of the All Ordinaries. For readers following ASX AI Stocks, the development adds a fresh reference point.

## What launched this week

The Nuix Neo AI Agent, released this week, lets users ask plain-language questions of very large collections of unstructured data such as emails and chat logs. It reads documents, images and other items, and follows links between people, accounts, communications and transactions.

The agent works across whole case inventories using a broad set of tools within the Neo platform, with role-based access controls enforced throughout. It also writes the knowledge graph queries automatically, so users do not need to build them by hand.

Timing is notable. The launch arrived within days of a wave of cooling sentiment toward AI infrastructure names on the local market, which makes application vendors with real customers a different kind of story from data centre builders.

## The audit trail pitch

The core appeal is traceability. Every answer links back to its source material, the agent records the steps it takes, and investigators can export the full conversation including steps and findings. Outputs are designed to be checked against the underlying documents rather than trusted on faith.

That design reflects a real concern in legal and regulatory work. A generative model that produces a confident but unsupported statement is a liability when the output may be tested in court, so a visible chain of reasoning is a practical requirement rather than a nice extra.

The same logic applies in banks and insurers. Compliance teams reviewing suspicious activity must be able to show why an alert was raised or dismissed, and a model that cannot show its reasoning does not meet that standard.

## How the framework fits together

The agent runs on the Neo Generative AI Framework, which connects a customer's chosen supported language model to Nuix's own data intelligence layer. That separation lets organisations choose a model that suits their security and cost needs while keeping the investigative data processing within Nuix's engine.

## Who the product targets

The release names enterprises, legal teams, auditors, regulators and law enforcement as the audience. The company says government agencies, law firms, financial institutions, corporations and regulators around the world already rely on its platform.

## The latest annual result

When it reported in August, Nuix showed annual revenue growth of just under an another, statutory earnings against a deficit the year before, and sharply higher adjusted operating earnings. Underlying cash flow surged.

Annualised contract value rose too, landing within the company's guided range. For a software business the contract value figure is the better guide to future revenue, because it captures the recurring commitments already signed.

## Neo as the growth engine

Contract value linked to Neo rose by a very large multiple of its former level and now accounts for close to an another of the total. Management describes Neo as the main growth driver, with a shift from individual features towards platform value.

## The regulatory overhang

The result also carried a legal update. Claims brought by the corporate regulator against the company and its former board members were dismissed, and the dismissal for the individuals is final. An appeal relating to the company itself remains pending.

## Outlook for the coming year

Management set a target range for contract value that points to continued growth, and said operating earnings should be similar to the year just ended after an isolated accelerated research spend. Most growth is expected in the period to June, in line with renewal cycles.

That weighting matters for the near-term share price. If the period to December looks flat, patience will be required, and the stock may react to quarterly updates rather than to product launches.

## Share price and market position

The shares have fallen over the past year and lagged the wider market, despite the improved result. The company sits within the broader All Ordinaries universe and is a smaller player than the global software names it competes with for attention.

A software stock that has been derated can look inexpensive on earnings multiples, but the market is waiting for proof that the new products translate into revenue and that the legal overhang clears.

## Where agentic AI fits

Within the wider ASX AI Stocks theme, Nuix is a pure application play rather than a hardware or infrastructure story. Its value depends on turning model capability into a product that regulated customers can trust.

The term agentic describes systems that plan and carry out multi-step tasks rather than answering a single question. That is useful for investigations, which are inherently multi-step, but it also raises the stakes for error and for oversight.

## Risks in the approach

Language models can produce plausible mistakes, and an investigative setting is unforgiving. The audit trail reduces the risk but does not remove it, and the company itself notes that outputs are meant to support, not replace, professional judgment.

## What to watch

Customer adoption of the agent, any pricing changes tied to the feature and the next update on contract value are the main signals. The appeal outcome is a separate but important event.

If Neo continues to grow at the pace of the last year and the legal issue fades, the narrative could shift from recovery to expansion. If adoption is slow, the launch will be remembered as an incremental feature rather than a turning point.

# Dubai Chambers launches world’s first chamber-led Agentic AI marketplace to ease access to Agentic AI solutions

Dubai Chambers members can now choose the AI Agent most relevant to their business needs and subscribe to the available packages with competitive benefits

The program aims to enable more than 295,000 private sector companies and roll out 100 specialized AI agents over two years

Dubai Chambers announced on Monday the launch of “Chamber AI Hub,” the world’s first chamber-led Agentic AI marketplace, enabling companies operating in Dubai to access ready-to-use, specialized Agentic AI solutions that can perform a wide range of administrative and operational tasks.

The initiative contributes to transforming corporate operating models and enhancing the competitiveness of Dubai’s private sector.

The launch of the Agentic AI marketplace comes as part of the implementation of the directives of H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, to accelerate the adoption of Agentic AI across Dubai’s private sector, which is overseen by Dubai Chambers.

## Platform to offer 22 specialized AI agents

The platform currently provides companies with access to 22 specialized AI agents across seven functional areas, including Compliance, Procurement, Operations, Finance, Sales, Human Resources and Logistics, with plans to expand the offering to 100 AI agents.

Dubai Chambers members can now choose the AI Agent most relevant to their business needs and subscribe to the available packages with competitive benefits.

“Success in the transition to Agentic AI is measured not by technology adoption alone, but by how effectively companies use these tools to address business challenges and deliver tangible results. This is why we are connecting knowledge with practical application, building capabilities, and expanding access to specialized solutions and high-quality tools that help companies adapt to change and evolve the way they work. Through this approach, we are preparing a private sector that is equipped to respond to technological transformation and contribute to shaping the opportunities of the future economy,” said H.E. Eng. Sultan bin Saeed Al Mansoori, Chairman of Dubai Chambers.

## Program to roll out 100 specialized AI agents over two years

The program aims to enable more than 295,000 private sector companies and roll out 100 specialized AI agents over two years. It also features specialized training tracks recently launched by Dubai Chambers to enable and train 14,000 companies from the Business Groups and Business Councils operating under the Dubai Chamber of Commerce to deploy Agentic AI technologies within their administrative and operational processes.

The program also includes supporting the growth of companies specializing in the development and use of Agentic AI solutions, promoting knowledge-sharing, and building institutional capabilities across the Dubai Chambers ecosystem.

The platform currently features 22 agents, each designed to perform specific tasks. The solutions support tasks including supplier discovery and evaluation of vendor proposals, monitoring supply chain risks, contract review, matching invoices against purchase orders, generating business proposals, screening resumes, lead scoring and handling IT help desk requests, among others.

## Dashboards to provide visibility into usage levels and costs

Developed by Dubai Chambers, the platform enables companies to try any AI agent in a sandbox before activating it. Companies also receive complimentary credits to get started, with the option to move to paid packages based on usage thereafter.

Dashboards provide visibility into usage levels and costs, while a readiness assessment helps companies determine their preparedness to use these solutions. The platform also provides visibility into success rates in fulfilling requests submitted to each AI agent. A company admin portal enables company administrators to monitor their teams’ use of AI agents.

The platform complies with all relevant regulatory requirements in the UAE and observes data privacy and protection standards. Data is hosted in the UAE, with each company’s information kept separate from that of other companies. The AI agents available through the platform support both Arabic and English.

# AI成为生产力，钛动科技发布营销业首个Pro级智能体

2026-10-26 16:26 来源: 南方Plus客户端

发布于：广东省

10月23日，以“AI is Profitable ”为主题的2026 TGC科技增长大会于广州召开，会上正式发布行业首个Pro Agent——Navos Pro。

钛动科技创始人、CEO李述昊谈到，将AI商业机会落在企业长期、持续投入的营销和销售、编程和产品开发、管理三笔费用上，对应提出AI for Growth、AI for Innovation与AI for Administration，三者预计构成AI for Work数万亿美元的广阔市场。在这一AI for Work三费框架中，Claude Code等AI产品主攻AI for Innovation，WorkBuddy等AI产品专注协同办公；而钛动科技的Navos Pro则将是AI for Growth的玩家。

李述昊进一步明确：“只做结果导向的 AI for Work ”。作为下一代 Agent，Navos Pro具备Professional、Proactive、Profitable三大能力体系，面向跨境电商、外贸、营销、商业分析等场景推进智能体落地：

三大体系背后，有着三层能力供给：Professional能力体系融合行业Know-How（知识技巧）与专属数据，形成数据库、Agent、工作流、互动四大能力：以公域数据、领域Benchmark和垂直场景提供趋势、竞品、选品、素材与投放洞察；以70+ MCP、100+ Skill和用户反馈持续调优；以Skill、Template、数字员工，把选品、素材创作、广告诊断等流程标准化、自动化；以意图识别、结果反馈和过程可溯源保障互动。

Proactive能力体系覆盖日均10亿+感知数据、2亿+感知频次，支持千万+广告诊断、百万+行动建议和10万+建议采纳，围绕账户、商品、素材主动监测，输出预算、出价、卖点和素材迭代建议，并联动Agent或人工执行。

Profitable能力体系以“批量创编、规模测试—规模生产、去伪存真—策略迭代、放大收益”推进，通过Learning Loop形成结果反馈、策略优化、持续进化闭环。

依托上述三大Pro体系，Navos已完整覆盖出海营销链路，同时设置Navos Lite和Navos Pro双版本矩阵。

李述昊表示，Agent 演进的本质是工作发起权的转移：Chatbot 阶段，AI被动应答；Copilot阶段，AI辅助执行；到了Pro-Agent阶段，AI开始主动发现业务机会并交付真实增长，Navos Pro将是这一阶段的代表。

钛动科技还启动 Pro-Agent Global Challenge 全球挑战赛，面向全球 AI 创业者征集 AI 前沿项目。大赛聚焦 Agent 架构演进、AI 营销、AI 内容入口与算力基础设施等赛道，并将开放资本、产业资源及全球增长通道为项目赋能。

# Armada & Johnson Controls to Deploy 500MW of Compute in 2027

October 26, 2026

undefined mins

Armada will build distributed sovereign superintelligence capacity in months, not years, says Dan Wright, Co-founder and CEO of Armada

Armada has announced it will partner with Johnson Controls to build 500MW of distributed sovereign superintelligence capacity in 2027.

The company plans to manufacture and deploy standardised superintelligence infrastructure built within the NVIDIA DSX POD reference design for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform.

This move aims to counter traditional data centre construction timelines, which can take years for a single facility to become IT-ready.

Armada highlights that a conventional 50MW facility can consume roughly 600,000 on-site labour hours, compounding a construction industry shortfall projected to reach 288,000 workers by 2027.

Together with Johnson Controls, Armada is positioned to bring Vera Rubin-based factories to customers who need capacity now, wherever their energy and data are.

### Factory-built superintelligence infrastructure

Armada will use the NVIDIA DSX POD, a reference design for standardised, factory-integrated compute containers, to accelerate the deployment of superintelligence capacity.

The design moves repeatable construction work from job sites into Armada’s Galleon Forge factories.

Here, compute, networking, rack-level power, liquid-cooling plumbing and supporting infrastructure are integrated and validated before shipment.

Once on site, Armada connects the containers to prepared power, water, cooling and networking.

This allows customers to scale by adding standardised containers as demand grows.

“The superintelligence race isn't going to be won by whoever pours concrete the fastest,” says Dan Wright, Co-founder and CEO of Armada.

“Companies and nations can have the chips, the land, the power, and the ambition, and still be told to wait years for a building.

“The NVIDIA DSX POD reference design lets us cut that wait out of the equation.

“We build the superintelligence factory in one of our Galleon Forge factories, ship it, connect it, and our customers are generating tokens in months, on infrastructure they own and control.”

In a LinkedIn Post, Dan added: "The payoff goes beyond speed. Capacity that goes live sooner means tokens flowing sooner, which drives returns for companies and shapes how competitive entire countries are in superintelligence, including their security and economic output.
"If America is going to win the superintelligence race, it can’t wait on concrete. It has to deploy infrastructure where energy already lives."

At a Glance: Armada’s distributed superintelligence factories

- Planned capacity: Armada and Johnson Controls plan to build 500MW of distributed sovereign superintelligence capacity in 2027.
- Deployment speed: The factory-built modular approach aims to reduce deployment times from years to months.
- Core technology: The facilities will be built using the NVIDIA DSX POD reference design for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform.
- Sovereign control: Each site is built on an open architecture with zero cloud dependencies, giving customers full ownership of their models, data and infrastructure.
- Construction bottleneck: The initiative addresses a projected construction industry shortfall of 288,000 workers by 2027.

## The role of NVIDIA’s DSX platform

Armada uses the NVIDIA DSX platform across the full life of a superintelligence factory.

This includes using NVIDIA DSX Air to simulate the facility and validate its Bridge GPU management software before hardware ships.

The company then uses the DSX POD reference design to manufacture the containers.

Once operational, NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS helps maximise token output within each site’s power envelope through software-driven power allocation, advanced performance-per-Watt techniques and power-envelope optimisation.

The Armada Platform also supports NVIDIA AI Grid, enabling operators and enterprises to manage geographically distributed AI infrastructure.

Under the collaboration, NVIDIA designs, tests and validates the DSX POD reference design for its Vera Rubin platform.

Armada then engineers, manufactures, integrates and delivers the modular data centres to customers at scale.

“The demand for compute is outpacing the speed at which the world can build the facilities to house it,” says Charlie Boyle, vice president of DGX Systems at NVIDIA.

“By utilising the NVIDIA DSX POD reference design, Armada can deliver factory-built, Vera Rubin-based containers to customers.

"Together with Johnson Controls, Armada is positioned to bring Vera Rubin-based factories to customers who need capacity now, wherever their energy and data are.”

## Manufacturing and deployment expertise

Armada’s experience includes deploying data centres in challenging environments such as frozen Alaska, a US Navy littoral combat ship and desert sites in the Middle East.

This work has informed its supply chain and engineering approach.

The company’s modular data centre readiness is achieved in partnership with Johnson Controls, while its superintelligence factory line is designed directly with NVIDIA and in line with NVIDIA reference architectures.

“NVIDIA is rapidly advancing the age of intelligence and reshaping the infrastructure required to support it,” says Joakim Weidemanis, CEO of Johnson Controls.

“Our collaboration with Armada combines their expertise in deploying compute at the edge with Johnson Controls' advanced thermal management technology, engineering capabilities and global manufacturing scale.

"This combination delivers high-performance infrastructure engineered to quickly bring capacity online where and when it's needed.”

If America is going to win the superintelligence race, it can’t wait on concrete. It has to deploy infrastructure where energy already lives.

## Key Project Partners

- NVIDIA: Provides the core architecture, designing, testing and validating the DSX POD reference design for the Vera Rubin platform.
- Johnson Controls: Delivers advanced thermal management technology, engineering capabilities and global manufacturing scale to the partnership.
- Armada: Acts as the primary integrator, engineering, manufacturing, customising, servicing and delivering the completed modular data centres to customers.

cross_cutting.description: Nvidia became a Preferred Nvidia Cloud Partner in August, ordering approximately $1 billion of Nvidia systems. ... The deal gave SWI 15 crypto data centers in the US and Sweden, with a footprint of 1.3GW of available power for potential conversion to AI data center sites.
cross_cutting.content:
# SWI launches AI cloud unit SWI Compute

Company launching with 30MW at group's planned Cambridge development

European real estate investor SWI has launched its new AI cloud division, SWI Compute.

SWI said its new compute division is supported by 3.6GW of power capacity across 24 sites in the US and Europe that the wider group has secured.

SWI Compute will deploy globally, with a focus on Europe. Its first large-scale deployment will be located in Cambridge, UK.

Starting with 30MW and hosting close to 7,000 Rubin GPUs and 3,500 Vera CPUs in Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, the site expected to come online by the end of 2027.

This 30MW is the initial phase of a UK campus planned to grow to 530MW, with the company targeting 2.3GW of Nvidia-focused capacity by 2029.

Nvidia became a Preferred Nvidia Cloud Partner in August, ordering approximately $1 billion of Nvidia systems. The firm said it has finalized contracts with its first customers.

"Energy availability represents the primary bottleneck facing European AI infrastructure. Having spent six years acquiring grid access, SWI Group is now deploying these power resources into dedicated Nvidia AI factories through SWI Compute," said Halil Mirakhmedov, CEO, SWI Compute. “Just two months after joining the Nvidia Cloud Partner program, our team secured approximately $1 billion in advanced hardware orders and executed initial client contracts. The market continues to surpass available capacity, and we are rapidly expanding our footprint to fulfill this requirement.”

SWI added that every SWI Compute site is built to Nvidia reference architectures, and going forward will be designed, built, and operated to Nvidia’s DSX AI Factory Platform requirements.

"AI factories are essential infrastructure that turn regional energy into intelligence and economic opportunity," said Nico Caprez, Vice President, global AI infrastructure growth at Nvidia. "SWI Compute is putting Europe's energy to work for the ecosystem of AI natives, labs, universities, and enterprises. Built on Nvidia reference architectures and adopting Nvidia DSX for its next generation of AI factories, SWI Compute is building infrastructure that is productive, durable, and fungible – able to serve new customers and workloads and keep generating value for years to come."

Formed from the merger of Stoneweg and Icona Capital last year, Euronext Amsterdam SWI Group has some €11 billion ($12.27bn) in assets under management.

The firm last year announced it was launching its own data center fund and platform, taking a stake in AiOnX, which has projects across the UK, Ireland, and mainland Europe.

AiOnX is developing a data center park in Cambridge, UK, and near Dublin in Ireland. The company also lists projects in Milan, Italy; Varde, Denmark; and Madrid, Spain. The Irish site is reportedly leased to Amazon.

Plans for SWI to launch a GPU-as-a-service provider were announced over the summer, though few details had been shared. The company was previously set to invest in German cloud and data center firm Polarise, but backed out to instead merely provide financing.

In the US, SWI recently acquired cryptominer Genesis Digital Assets and rebranded it to SWI Digital. The deal gave SWI 15 crypto data centers in the US and Sweden, with a footprint of 1.3GW of available power for potential conversion to AI data center sites.

"We started investing in land, power, and shell in 2020. SWI Compute is the final piece, providing fully integrated infrastructure for Nvidia AI factories. SWI Group is now a transatlantic, vertically integrated digital infrastructure company, from the grid connection to the GPU, and SWI Compute puts that capacity directly in the hands of the customers who need it most," said Max-Hervé George, founder and CEO, SWI Group.

SWI’s Stoneweg Europe Stapled Trust (SERT), which combines Stoneweg European Real Estate Investment Trust and Stoneweg European Business Trust, is also looking to potentially redevelop around ten industrial sites across four European countries for data center use.

Plans for SWI’s Cambridge site were announced in June 2025. The project is located at Sutton-in-the-Isle in Cambridgeshire.

cross_cutting.content:
# Cisco partners with Mannai to build sovereign AI infrastructure in Qatar

Cisco is advancing its sovereign AI infrastructure vision with a focus on supporting Qatar’s next phase of digital transformation.

Working alongside its longstanding technology partner, Mannai Corporation QPSC, through Mannai Technologies – Networking & ELV, Cisco’s approach brings together advanced computing, networking, cybersecurity and infrastructure management capabilities to address the growing demand for secure, resilient and locally controlled AI environments.

The initiative reflects the increasing importance of digital sovereignty as governments and enterprises accelerate AI adoption, placing greater emphasis on data control, operational independence and the security of critical digital infrastructure.

Cisco’s Sovereign Critical Infrastructure portfolio brings together integrated technologies across networking, security, collaboration and observability. Designed for customer-controlled environments, including on-premises and air-gapped deployments, the portfolio supports organisations seeking greater autonomy over the systems and data underpinning essential services.

For Qatar, such capabilities align with growing demand for AI-ready infrastructure across government, energy, financial services, healthcare and other critical sectors, alongside the country’s broader digital transformation ambitions under Qatar National Vision 2030.

The Cisco–Mannai relationship spans more than three decades of technology collaboration in Qatar. Mannai Technologies – Networking & ELV contributes local engineering, systems integration and deployment expertise, complementing Cisco’s global portfolio and helping organisations navigate complex infrastructure requirements.

Together, Cisco’s technology vision and Mannai’s established local capabilities provide a foundation for conversations around secure, resilient and sovereign AI infrastructure as Qatar prepares for its next phase of digital innovation.

cross_cutting.content:
# Freedom Holding is developing a $2bn sovereign AI hub in Kazakhstan

Freedom Holding will open its first public GPU cloud in 2027. Its CEO, Timur Turlov, met Nvidia’s Jensen Huang in Astana last week, on Huang’s first visit to the country.

Freedom Holding Corp. is developing the $2bn hub under an agreement signed in November 2025 with Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development, the Nasdaq-listed group said in a statement on Monday. The site is planned with 100MW of available power. Freedom is the main financing and delivery partner and will run the hub.

The hub is meant for AI model training, large-scale data processing and AI services for business and government. Demand already stands at twice the planned capacity of its first stage, according to Timur Turlov, Freedom’s chief executive. Major prospective clients have said they are willing to lease future capacity for five years, the company said.

## A public GPU cloud in 2027

Freedom plans to open its first GPU cluster to businesses and developers as a public cloud in 2027. A separate Freedom AI Super Cluster, for government, business and science, is due to start its first phase in the first quarter of 2027.

A new Freedom Cloud data centre is under construction near Almaty. Freedom Cloud already serves more than 3,400 business and public-sector clients. The wider group runs banking, brokerage, insurance and telecoms businesses, along with ticketing, travel, e-commerce and food delivery services.

## Jensen Huang in Astana

Turlov met Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang in Astana on 23 October, during Huang’s first visit to Kazakhstan. Turlov presented Freedom’s technology businesses and its AI plans, the company said. The statement does not name a chip supplier for the hub.

Turlov said Kazakhstan has built a strong pool of talent that already creates technology in e-commerce and finance. Combined with domestic AI infrastructure, he said, this is becoming one of the country’s main advantages.

Other governments are chasing the same goal. Nvidia and Palantir began selling a sovereign AI stack in September. Malaysia has weighed Huawei chips for its own push, Bloomberg reported. In Europe, research has warned that sovereign AI plans could stall on data centre limits.

# SWI Compute Emerges from Stealth to Turn Gigawatts of Power Into NVIDIA AI Factories, Starting in Europe

EQS-News: SWI Group / Key word(s): Expansion/Private Equity
SWI Compute Emerges from Stealth to Turn Gigawatts of Power Into NVIDIA AI Factories, Starting in Europe
26.10.2026 / 08:50 CET/CEST
The issuer is solely responsible for the content of this announcement.

SINGAPORE and AMSTERDAM, Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SWI Compute today emerged from stealth to build and operate NVIDIA AI factories, launching first in Europe. The global AI infrastructure company is backed by 3.6 gigawatts of power capacity that SWI Group has spent six years securing across Europe and the US. The new company of Euronext Amsterdam-listed SWI Group became a Preferred NVIDIA Cloud Partner in August, ordered approximately $1 billion of NVIDIA systems and has finalized contracts with its first customers. SWI Compute will deploy globally, with the strongest presence and deployments in Europe. Its first large-scale AI factory in the UK starts with 30 MW, close to 7,000 Rubin GPUs and 3,500 Vera CPUs in NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, expected to come online by the end of 2027. Connected by NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, these 30 MW are the initial phase of a UK campus planned to grow to 530 MW, and the first step towards 2.3 GW of NVIDIA AI factory capacity by 2029.

"Energy availability represents the primary bottleneck facing European AI infrastructure. Having spent six years acquiring grid access, SWI Group is now deploying these power resources into dedicated NVIDIA AI factories through SWI Compute. Just two months after joining the NVIDIA Cloud Partner program, our team secured approximately $1 billion in advanced hardware orders and executed initial client contracts. The market continues to surpass available capacity, and we are rapidly expanding our footprint to fulfill this requirement," said Halil Mirakhmedov, CEO, SWI Compute.

Europe has the researchers, the founders and the enterprises to build frontier AI. Much of that building has happened on capacity outside Europe, and the capacity that exists has been committed first to global hyperscalers and frontier labs, the buyers able to sign multi-year contracts at scale. The companies with the most urgent need, AI natives with frontier ambitions and startup balance sheets, have the hardest time securing it.

SWI Compute is built for them. It provides dedicated and on-demand access to NVIDIA AI factories for Europe's AI natives, AI labs and enterprises, close to their users and their data and under European jurisdiction, so the next generation of AI can be trained, fine-tuned and served where it is made. Its first customer, a US-based AI inference platform, has contracted capacity.

SWI Group began investing in land, power and shell in 2020. Today it holds 3.6 GW of power capacity across Europe and the US, with its deepest presence in Europe, where its five campuses are in Ireland, the UK, Denmark, Spain and Italy, one of them already leased to a major hyperscaler. The Group develops its own sites, from grid connection to commissioning. The power is contracted and the systems are on order.

Every SWI Compute site is built to NVIDIA reference architectures. Going forward, SWI Compute will design, build and operate its AI factories with the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, which codesigns compute, networking, power and cooling as one integrated system. Every new site from 2027, starting with its UK campus, will follow the NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory reference design. On NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, DSX can enable up to 40% more GPU capacity within the same power budget.

The first deployment runs NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra systems, with NVIDIA Vera CPU racks to follow, connected by NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet. From NVIDIA's OEM and ODM ecosystem, SWI Compute has selected its systems partners, with Delta Computers as systems integrator, alongside industry-recognized storage partners, to deliver more than 8,000 GPUs.

An AI factory earns on three things: how many tokens it produces per megawatt, how many years it keeps producing them, and how many kinds of work it can take on. Over time, continuous software optimization keeps installed systems earning years after they ship. Across workloads, the same infrastructure runs every type of AI in every phase, from pretraining to agentic inference, alongside simulation, data processing and scientific computing. For SWI Compute's customers, that is capacity that stays current. For SWI Group, it is an asset that stays productive.

"AI factories are essential infrastructure that turn regional energy into intelligence and economic opportunity," said Nico Caprez, Vice President, Global AI Infrastructure Growth at NVIDIA. "SWI Compute is putting Europe's energy to work for the ecosystem of AI natives, labs, universities and enterprises. Built on NVIDIA reference architectures and adopting NVIDIA DSX for its next generation of AI factories, SWI Compute is building infrastructure that is productive, durable and fungible—able to serve new customers and workloads and keep generating value for years to come."

The first AI factory marks just the beginning of SWI Compute's ambitious expansion strategy. Starting in Q4 2027, its next generation of AI campuses across Europe is scheduled to come online, with thousands of GPUs planned for deployment.

SWI Compute's competitive advantage lies in building AI cloud infrastructure on a power foundation already controlled by SWI Group, with access to up to 3.6 GW of power capacity across 24 sites.

This positions SWI Compute to scale rapidly, transforming the Group's existing energy infrastructure into a next-generation AI cloud platform.

"We started investing in land, power and shell in 2020. SWI Compute is the final piece, providing fully integrated infrastructure for NVIDIA AI factories. SWI Group is now a transatlantic, vertically integrated digital infrastructure company, from the grid connection to the GPU, and SWI Compute puts that capacity directly in the hands of the customers who need it most," said Max-Hervé George, Founder and CEO, SWI Group.

About SWI Compute

SWI Compute is an AI & infrastructure provider based in Europe and part of SWI Group (Euronext Amsterdam: SWICH). SWI Compute completes SWI Group's transatlantic vertically integrated AI stack by providing compute services with AiOnX's European campuses and SWI Digital's US data centers. Learn more at www.swi-compute.com and www.aionx.com.

About SWI Group

SWI Group (SWI Capital Holding Ltd) is a transatlantic investment group allocating more than 80% of its capital in digital infrastructure, listed on Euronext Amsterdam under ticker SWICH. Formed through the merger of Icona and Stoneweg, the Group deploys its own capital across primarily digital infrastructure, and real estate and other private-market opportunities, combining an entrepreneurial approach with institutional discipline. For more information, visit www.swi.com.
